knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded strict-descent criterion for variational equilibria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairs monotonicity with existence and strict monotonicity with unique existence in a shared-constraint game.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\theta_v(\cdot,x^{-v})\) is convex for every \(v\) and \(x^{-v}\), and that closed convex sets \(\mathbf C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(X^v\subset\mathbb R^{n_v}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{gph}(\Xi^v)=\{x\in\mathbf C:x^v\in X^v\}\) for every \(v\). If \(\partial\mathbf\Theta\) is monotone on \(\widehat{\mathbf C}\), then \(\mathcal G(\mathbf\Xi,\partial\mathbf\Theta)\) has a variational equilibrium if and only if there exists \(x^{\mathrm{ref}}\in\widehat{\mathbf C}\) such that \[\{y\in\widehat{\mathbf C}:\exists u\in\partial\mathbf\Theta(y),\ (y-x^{\mathrm{ref}})^Tu<0\}\] is bounded. If \(\partial\mathbf\Theta\) is strictly monotone on \(\widehat{\mathbf C}\), the same boundedness condition is equivalent to existence of a unique variational equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex shared-constraint game, monotonicity of the joint subdifferential makes existence of a variational equilibrium equivalent to boundedness of a strict-descent set relative to some reference point. Under strict monotonicity, the same condition is equivalent to unique existence.
assumptions_latex: \operatorname{gph}(\Xi^v)=\{x\in\mathbf C:x^v\in X^v\}\text{ for closed convex }\mathbf C,X^v

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-leader–multi-follower games and their separable bilevel reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition, nonunique-response boundary, and reduction to a single-follower bilevel problem when followers are uncoupled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a single-leader–multi-follower game, the leader chooses $x$ and the follower vector $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_M)$ must belong to the generalized Nash equilibrium set $\operatorname{GNEP}(x)$, where follower $j$ has feasible-set map $Y_j(x,y_{-j})$. If no follower objective or constraint map depends on another follower's decision, so that follower $j$ minimizes $f_j(y_j,x)$ over $Y_j(x)$, define $f(x,y)=\sum_{j=1}^M f_j(y_j,x)$ and $Y(x)=\{y:y_j\in Y_j(x)\ \forall j\}$. Then the model is equivalently a classical bilevel problem with the single aggregated follower variable $y$, objective $f$, and feasible set $Y(x)$. If $\operatorname{GNEP}(x)$ is not single-valued and no response-selection convention is specified, the leader's anticipated-response problem is ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-leader–multi-follower game constrains the followers to a generalized Nash equilibrium parameterized by the leader's decision. When followers' objectives and constraints are mutually independent, their problems aggregate into one separable follower problem, yielding an equivalent ordinary bilevel formulation. Without a rule for selecting among multiple follower equilibria, the leader's problem is ambiguous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{y\in Y(x)}\sum_{j=1}^M f_j(y_j,x)=\prod_{j=1}^M\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{y_j\in Y_j(x)}f_j(y_j,x),\quad\text{while nonunique }\operatorname{GNEP}(x)\text{ requires a response-selection convention.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness of a Normalized Generalized Nash Equilibrium
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameterized NGNE system under the source-defined assumptions A3 and A4.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume A3 and A4. Let \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}_+^2\) be convex, and suppose that, for every \(r\in Q\), \(\sigma(y,z;x,r)\) is diagonally strictly convex uniformly with respect to \(x\in X\). Then, for every \(r\in Q\), there exists a unique normalized generalized Nash equilibrium point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under assumptions A3 and A4, if the equilibrium mapping sigma is diagonally strictly convex uniformly over x for every parameter r in a convex subset of the positive orthant, then every such r admits exactly one normalized generalized Nash equilibrium point.
assumptions_latex: \forall r\in Q,\;\sigma(y,z;x,r)\text{ is diagonally strictly convex uniformly in }x\in X.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall r\in Q,\;\exists!\text{ a normalized generalized Nash equilibrium point.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: P-property and strict-monotonicity uniqueness criteria for game equilibria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives separate uniqueness guarantees for product-feasible Nash equilibria and shared-constraint variational equilibria.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that \(\theta_v(\cdot,x^{-v})\) is convex for every player \(v\) and every \(x^{-v}\). (a) If each response set is independent of rivals, \(\Xi^v(x^{-v})=X^v\), with \(X^v\) closed and convex, and \(\partial\mathbf\Theta\) has the P-property on \(\widehat X=\prod_vX^v\), then \(\mathcal G(\widehat X,\partial\mathbf\Theta)\) has at most one Nash equilibrium. (b) If closed convex sets \(\mathbf C\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(X^v\subset\mathbb R^{n_v}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{gph}(\Xi^v)=\{x\in\mathbf C:x^v\in X^v\}\) for every \(v\), and \(\partial\mathbf\Theta\) is strictly monotone on \(\mathbf C\cap\widehat X\), then \(\mathcal G(\mathbf\Xi,\partial\mathbf\Theta)\) has at most one variational equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex player objectives, the joint subdifferential's P-property yields uniqueness of a Nash equilibrium over independent closed convex strategy sets. With shared closed convex constraints, strict monotonicity of the joint subdifferential yields uniqueness of a variational equilibrium.
assumptions_latex: \text{(b) }\operatorname{gph}(\Xi^v)=\{x\in\mathbf C:x^v\in X^v\}\text{ for closed convex }\mathbf C,X^v
\text{(b) }\partial\mathbf\Theta\text{ is strictly monotone on }\mathbf C\cap\widehat X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(a) }|\operatorname{NE}(\mathcal G(\widehat X,\partial\mathbf\Theta))|\le1;\qquad \text{(b) }|\operatorname{VE}(\mathcal G(\mathbf\Xi,\partial\mathbf\Theta))|\le1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cournot Oligopoly First-Order Conditions as a Variational Inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-cone generalized-equation representation of firms' first-order conditions, with own-output concavity required for equivalence to Cournot optimal-response conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let N=\{1,\ldots,n\}, let each Y_i\subset\mathbb R_+ be a nonempty closed interval, set Y=\prod_{i=1}^nY_i and T=\sum_{i=1}^ny_i, and define u_i(y)=y_ip(T)-f_i(y_i). Then the firms' first-order conditions can be written as 0\in-\mathcal M(y)+N_Y(y), where \mathcal M_i(y)=\nabla_{y_i}u_i(y)=p(T)+y_ip'(T)-f_i'(y_i). If each u_i(\cdot,y_{-i}) is concave on Y_i, this generalized equation is equivalent to the firms' individual optimal-response conditions and hence characterizes Cournot equilibria.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The firms' first-order conditions form a normal-cone generalized equation whose mapping is marginal profit. If every firm's profit is concave in its own output, this system is equivalent to the firms' optimal-response conditions and characterizes Cournot equilibrium. Convex costs contribute the cost-side concavity but do not alone establish profit concavity.
assumptions_latex: N=\{1,\ldots,n\},\quad Y_i\subset\mathbb R_+\text{ is a nonempty closed interval for every }i
\text{For equivalence to optimal-response conditions, }u_i(\cdot,y_{-i})\text{ is concave on }Y_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in-\mathcal M(y)+N_Y(y),\qquad \mathcal M_i(y)=p(T)+y_ip'(T)-f_i'(y_i),\quad\text{and under own-output concavity this characterizes Cournot equilibrium.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Concavity of Residual-Demand Revenue
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A curvature criterion for strict concavity of a firm's revenue as a function of its own output when rivals' aggregate output is fixed and positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose p\in C^2(\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+) is strictly convex and the function \vartheta\mapsto\vartheta p(\vartheta) is concave. Then, for every K>0, the function g_K(\vartheta)=\vartheta p(\vartheta+K) is strictly concave on \operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If inverse demand is twice continuously differentiable and strictly convex while total revenue θp(θ) is concave, then for every positive fixed rival supply K, the residual-demand revenue θp(θ+K) is strictly concave in own output.
assumptions_latex: p\text{ is strictly convex on }\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \vartheta\mapsto\vartheta p(\vartheta+K)\text{ is strictly concave on }\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Priced QoS communication game
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the secondary-user optimization problems and the primary-user interference-pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P,Q,N\in\mathbb N. Given rivals' allocations x_{-q} and nonnegative prices, secondary user q chooses x_q\ge 0 to minimize \[\sum_{k=1}^N x_q(k)+\sum_{p=1}^P\sum_{k=1}^N\bigl(\lambda_p(k)+\lambda_{p,\mathrm{tot}}\bigr)\beta_{p,q}(k)x_q(k)\] subject to \[\sum_{k=1}^N\log\!\left(1+\frac{x_q(k)}{\widehat\sigma_q^2(k)+\sum_{r\ne q}\widehat h_{qr}(k)x_r(k)}\right)\ge L_q.\] For each p,k, the primary-user prices satisfy \[0\le\lambda_p(k)\perp \alpha_p(k)-\sum_{q=1}^Q\beta_{p,q}(k)x_q(k)\ge0,\] \[0\le\lambda_{p,\mathrm{tot}}\perp \alpha_{p,\mathrm{tot}}-\sum_{k=1}^N\sum_{q=1}^Q\beta_{p,q}(k)x_q(k)\ge0.\] Equivalently, these prices minimize over nonnegative \lambda the linear objective obtained by multiplying each interference slack by its corresponding price.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each secondary user minimizes transmit power plus interference charges while meeting a minimum-rate QoS constraint. Primary users choose nonnegative per-band and aggregate interference prices through complementary slackness, equivalently by minimizing a linear function of the interference slacks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The coupled secondary-user programs and primary-user price program define the priced QoS communication game.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree One Near a Strictly Semicopositive Nash Equilibrium
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local topological degree of the game's normal map under the hypotheses of Proposition 12.14.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that for every player \(v\), \(X^v\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_v}\) is closed and convex, \(\theta_v(\cdot,x^{-v})\) is convex for every \(x^{-v}\), and \(\theta_v\) is twice continuously differentiable. Let \(x^*\) be a Nash equilibrium such that \(\mathbf M(x^*)\) is strictly semicopositive on \(\mathcal C(x^*)\). Then there exists an open neighborhood \(\Omega\) of \(x^*\) such that \[\deg(\mathbf N^{\mathcal G};\Omega)=1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the closed-convex, own-strategy convexity, smoothness, and strict-semicopositivity assumptions, the game's normal map has topological degree one on an open neighborhood of the Nash equilibrium.
assumptions_latex: \forall v,\ X^v\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_v}\text{ is closed and convex}

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\,\Omega\text{ open with }x^*\in\Omega\text{ such that }\deg(\mathbf N^{\mathcal G};\Omega)=1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Definiteness Criterion for Uniform Diagonal Strict Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient matrix condition at a fixed positive parameter under the source-defined assumptions A3 and A4.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume A3 and A4 and fix \(r=\bar r>0\). If \(P(y,z;x,\bar r)+P(y,z;x,\bar r)^{\top}\) is positive definite uniformly with respect to \(x\in X\) for every \((y,z)\in\Theta(x)\), then \(\sigma(y,z;x,\bar r)\) is diagonally strictly convex on \(\Theta(x)\), uniformly with respect to \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under assumptions A3 and A4, at a fixed positive parameter, uniform positive definiteness of the symmetric part of P over every feasible set Theta(x) is sufficient for sigma to be diagonally strictly convex uniformly over x.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma(y,z;x,\bar r)\text{ is diagonally strictly convex on }\Theta(x)\text{ uniformly with respect to }x\in X.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded strict-descent criterion for Nash-equilibrium existence and uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes equilibrium existence under the P0-property and unique existence under the P-property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every \(X^v\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_v}\) be closed and convex, let \(\widehat X=\prod_vX^v\), and suppose \(\theta_v(\cdot,x^{-v})\) is convex for every \(x^{-v}\). For \(x^{\mathrm{ref}}\in\widehat X\), define \[\widehat L_{<}(x^{\mathrm{ref}})=\left\{y\in\widehat X:\ \forall v\text{ with }y^v\ne x^{\mathrm{ref},v},\ \exists u^v\in\partial_{x^v}\theta_v(y)\text{ such that }(y^v-x^{\mathrm{ref},v})^Tu^v<0\right\}.\] (a) If \(\partial\mathbf\Theta\) has the \(P_0\)-property on \(\widehat X\), then \(\mathcal G(\widehat X,\partial\mathbf\Theta)\) has a Nash equilibrium if and only if some \(x^{\mathrm{ref}}\in\widehat X\) makes \(\widehat L_{<}(x^{\mathrm{ref}})\) bounded. (b) If \(\partial\mathbf\Theta\) has the P-property on \(\widehat X\), then the game has a unique Nash equilibrium if and only if such a reference vector exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex game on closed convex product strategy sets, a Nash equilibrium exists under the P0-property exactly when the strict blockwise descent set is bounded for some reference point. Under the P-property, the same boundedness condition is equivalent to existence of a unique Nash equilibrium.
assumptions_latex: X^v\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_v}\text{ is closed and convex for every }v
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{(a) }\operatorname{NE}\ne\varnothing\iff\exists x^{\mathrm{ref}}\in\widehat X:\widehat L_{<}(x^{\mathrm{ref}})\text{ is bounded};\quad \text{(b) }|\operatorname{NE}|=1\iff\exists x^{\mathrm{ref}}\in\widehat X:\widehat L_{<}(x^{\mathrm{ref}})\text{ is bounded}

children.title: Network Equilibria as VIs
children.top_down_role: VI formulations for flow, traffic, and network equilibrium systems.

assumptions_latex: A directed network has a nonempty closed convex feasible flow set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^A\).
The arc-cost map \(c:K\to\mathbb R^A\) is continuous.
Users are nonatomic and select feasible routes of minimum experienced cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible flow is a Wardrop equilibrium exactly when it solves \(\operatorname{VI}(K,c)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static nonatomic routing equilibrium in arc-flow form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) encode flow conservation, nonnegativity, and fixed origin-destination demands. A feasible flow \(x^*\in K\) is a Wardrop equilibrium when every used route has minimum cost among routes serving the same demand pair. In aggregate arc-flow variables this equilibrium condition is equivalent to
\[
\langle c(x^*),x-x^*\rangle
=\sum_{a\in A}c_a(x^*)(x_a-x_a^*)\geq0
\quad\text{for every }x\in K.
\]
Thus the network equilibrium is represented by \(\operatorname{VI}(K,c)\); uniqueness of the aggregate flow additionally follows when \(c\) is strictly monotone on \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Wardrop traffic equilibrium is the VI asserting that no feasible aggregate flow has lower cost in the equilibrium cost vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Equilibria as VIs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the route-based Wardrop condition requires explicit assumptions connecting route costs, arc costs, feasible path flows, and aggregate arc flows. The strict-monotonicity uniqueness claim also requires source support.

children.title: Network Games as VI Models
children.top_down_role: VI models combining strategic interaction with network structure.

assumptions_latex: Player \(i\) chooses a network action \(x_i\) from a nonempty closed convex set, with joint feasible set \(K\).
Each cost \(J_i(x_i,x_{-i})\) is differentiable and convex in the player's own action.
Shared network effects enter the costs or the joint feasible constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every variational network equilibrium solves the VI on \(K\) induced by the game pseudo-gradient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex differentiable network games, including shared constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
F(x):=\bigl(\nabla_{x_1}J_1(x),\ldots,\nabla_{x_N}J_N(x)\bigr).
\]
A variational network equilibrium is a point \(x^*\in K\) satisfying
\[
\langle F(x^*),x-x^*\rangle
=\sum_i\left\langle\nabla_{x_i}J_i(x^*),x_i-x_i^*\right\rangle\geq0
\quad\text{for every }x\in K.
\]
When \(K=\prod_iX_i\), this condition is equivalent to Nash equilibrium under own-action convexity. For shared constraints, it selects the generalized Nash equilibria whose players use a common multiplier for the shared constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex network game is modeled by the VI of its pseudo-gradient; shared constraints select the common-multiplier variational equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Games as VI Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-set VI model is standard, but the shared-constraint claim about generalized Nash equilibria and common multipliers depends on a precise variational-equilibrium definition and constraint qualification. No inspectable source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity, compactness, and quasiconvexity assumptions for an MLMFG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assumptions used for an existence result with a unique follower response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every leader profile $x$, suppose the lower level has a unique response $y(x)$. For every leader $i$, suppose $F_i$ and $y$ are continuous; there is a nonempty compact convex set $K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}$ such that $X_i:K_i\rightrightarrows K_{-i}$ is upper and lower semicontinuous with nonempty closed convex values, where $K_{-i}:=\prod_{k\ne i}K_k$; and $\widetilde F_i(x):=F_i(x,y(x))$ is quasiconvex in $x_i$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every leader profile has a unique follower response. Each leader objective and the response map are continuous; each leader has a nonempty compact convex strategy set and a continuous feasible-set correspondence with nonempty closed convex values; and each reduced leader objective is quasiconvex in that leader's strategy.
assumptions_latex: \forall x\;\exists!\,y(x)\text{ solving the lower-level response problem}
\forall i,\quad \varnothing\ne K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\text{ is compact and convex}
\forall i,\quad X_i:K_i\rightrightarrows K_{-i},\quad K_{-i}:=\prod_{k\ne i}K_k,\text{ is upper and lower semicontinuous with nonempty closed convex values}
\forall i,\quad \widetilde F_i(x):=F_i(x,y(x))\text{ is quasiconvex with respect to }x_i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Conditions (A1)--(A4) hold for the reduced multi-leader game.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of an Optimistic SLMFG Equilibrium
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An attainment result for a single-leader multi-follower game whose lower level is a GNEP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume: (i) \(F\) is lower semicontinuous and \(X\) is closed; (ii) \(f_j\) is continuous for every \(j=1,\ldots,M\); (iii) for every \(j\), \(\operatorname{Dom}Y_j\neq\varnothing\), \(g_j\) is continuous on \(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\), and MFCQ holds at every feasible point; and (iv) either \(F\) is coercive, or \(X\) is compact and the images of \(Y_j\) are uniformly bounded for at least one \(j\). If the graph of the lower-level GNEP is nonempty, then the SLMFG admits an optimistic equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the leader objective is lower semicontinuous, the leader set is closed, all follower objectives and constraints have the stated continuity and feasibility properties, MFCQ holds at every feasible point, and the stated coercivity or compactness-and-boundedness alternative holds, then a nonempty lower-level GNEP graph guarantees an optimistic equilibrium.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is lower semicontinuous and }X\text{ is closed}
\forall j,\ \operatorname{Dom}Y_j\neq\varnothing,\quad g_j\in C(\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m),\quad \text{MFCQ holds at every feasible point}
F\text{ is coercive}\ \lor\ \bigl(X\text{ is compact and }\exists j\text{ such that the images of }Y_j\text{ are uniformly bounded}\bigr)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The SLMFG admits an optimistic equilibrium.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of a multi-leader-multi-follower game solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence under unique follower response, continuity, compact-convex feasible correspondences, and leaderwise quasiconvexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that for every leader profile $x$ the lower level has a unique response $y(x)$; for every $i$, $F_i$ and $y$ are continuous; there is a nonempty compact convex $K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}$ such that $X_i:K_i\rightrightarrows K_{-i}$ is upper and lower semicontinuous with nonempty closed convex values; and $\widetilde F_i(x):=F_i(x,y(x))$ is quasiconvex in $x_i$. Then the multi-leader-multi-follower game admits a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multi-leader-multi-follower game has a solution when follower responses are unique, the relevant objectives and response map are continuous, the leaders' feasible correspondences have nonempty closed convex values over compact convex strategy sets, and every reduced leader objective is quasiconvex in that leader's strategy.
assumptions_latex: \forall x\;\exists!\,y(x)\text{ solving the lower-level response problem}
\forall i,\quad \varnothing\ne K_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\text{ is compact and convex}
\forall i,\quad X_i:K_i\rightrightarrows K_{-i},\quad K_{-i}:=\prod_{k\ne i}K_k,\text{ is upper and lower semicontinuous with nonempty closed convex values}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Sol}(\mathrm{MLMFG})\ne\varnothing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniqueness and Asymptotic Equivalence of Parameterized MIMO Game Equilibria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of the equilibria of \(\mathcal G_\alpha\) and its limiting game \(\mathcal G_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\mathcal G_\alpha\) and \(\mathcal G_\infty\). Suppose that, for every \(q\in\Omega\), \(r_{\widehat U_a}<r_{H_{qq}}=n_{T_q}=n_{R_q}\), and that condition \((\mathrm C7)\) holds. Then both games have unique Nash equilibria, denoted \(Q_\alpha^\star\) and \(Q_\infty^\star\), and \[\lim_{\alpha\to+\infty}Q_\alpha^\star=Q_\infty^\star.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated rank hypothesis and condition (C7), both the parameterized MIMO game and its limiting game have unique Nash equilibria. The equilibrium of the parameterized game converges to the equilibrium of the limiting game as the parameter tends to infinity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists!Q_\alpha^\star,\ \exists!Q_\infty^\star,\qquad \lim_{\alpha\to+\infty}Q_\alpha^\star=Q_\infty^\star.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonemptiness of approximate solution sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two existence conclusions corresponding to the regularized maps \widetilde M^\varepsilon and M^\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume X is compact and L is lower semicontinuous on X\times Y. If X is closed, Y is convex and compact, F is continuous on X\times Y, and (C_1)-(C_4) hold, then \widetilde{\mathcal W}^{\varepsilon}\neq\varnothing for every \varepsilon>0. If, in addition, F(x,\cdot) is strictly quasiconvex on K(x) for every x\in X, then \mathcal W^{\varepsilon}\neq\varnothing for every \varepsilon>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compactness of the leader set and lower semicontinuity of the leader objective yield existence of every positive-tolerance approximate solution under the regularized reaction-map assumptions. Adding strict quasiconvexity of the objective on each follower feasible set gives the corresponding existence result for the second approximate solution set.
assumptions_latex: L\text{ is lower semicontinuous on }X\times Y
g_i\text{ is lower semicontinuous on }X\times Y\ \forall i
g_i(\cdot,y)\text{ is upper semicontinuous on }X\ \forall i,\forall y\in Y
g_i(x,\cdot)\text{ is strictly quasiconvex and upper semicontinuous on }Y\ \forall i,\forall x\in X
\forall x\in X\ \exists y\in Y:\ \max_{1\le i\le k}g_i(x,y)<0
F(x,\cdot)\text{ is strictly quasiconvex on }K(x)\ \forall x\in X\quad\text{(for the }\mathcal W^\varepsilon\text{ branch)}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\varepsilon>0:\ \widetilde{\mathcal W}^{\varepsilon}\neq\varnothing;\quad\text{under the additional strict-quasiconvexity assumption, }\mathcal W^{\varepsilon}\neq\varnothing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equilibrium existence under price, cost, and aggregate-response curvature conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence theorem for a Cournot-type MLMFG with a unique follower equilibrium response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $p$ be strictly decreasing and twice differentiable, with $p'(z)+zp''(z)\le 0$ for every $z\ge 0$. Let $c_i$ and $c_j$ be nonnegative, nondecreasing, convex, and twice differentiable, and suppose that some $z_u>0$ satisfies $c_i'(z)\ge p(z)$ and $c_j'(z)\ge p(z)$ for every $z\in[0,z_u]$. If $y(x)$ is the unique follower equilibrium response and $x\mapsto\sum_j y_j(x)$ is convex, then the MLMFG has at least one equilibrium.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Cournot-type multi-leader-multi-follower game has an equilibrium when inverse demand has the stated decreasing curvature, the relevant costs are nonnegative, nondecreasing, convex and twice differentiable with marginal costs dominating price on the specified interval, the follower equilibrium response is unique, and aggregate follower output is convex in the leaders' profile.
assumptions_latex: p\text{ is strictly decreasing and twice differentiable on }[0,\infty)
c_i,c_j\text{ are nonnegative, nondecreasing, convex, and twice differentiable}
\exists z_u>0\;\forall z\in[0,z_u],\quad c_i'(z)\ge p(z)\ \land\ c_j'(z)\ge p(z)
y(x)\text{ is the unique equilibrium response of the followers}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Eq}(\mathrm{MLMFG})\ne\varnothing

knowledge_statements.title: VIs as Equilibrium Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional optimization with a parameterized VI constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An optimization problem with a variational-inequality equilibrium constraint has the form
\[
\operatorname*{minimize}_{x,y}\ \Phi(x,y)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
x\in X,
\quad y\in K(x),
\quad \langle F(x,y),v-y\rangle\geq0\quad\text{for every }v\in K(x).
\]
Equivalently, its equilibrium constraint may be written as
\[
0\in F(x,y)+N_{K(x)}(y)
\]
or as \(y\in\operatorname{SOL}(K(x),F(x,\cdot))\). This equilibrium condition is part of the feasible-set definition of the upper-level problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An upper-level optimization problem has a VI equilibrium constraint when its lower-level variable is required to solve a parameterized VI.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the upper-level feasible set.
For every \(x\in X\), \(K(x)\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(F:X\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R^m\) defines the lower-level equilibrium field.
\(\Phi:X\times\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is the upper-level objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower-level constraint requires \(y\in\operatorname{SOL}(K(x),F(x,\cdot))\), producing an optimization problem with a VI equilibrium constraint.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subgradient Generation from Weakly Active Follower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-specific subgradient result for the specified Cournot equilibrium-constrained problem; numbered model definitions are retained as contextual assumptions because their formulas are not present in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the specified equilibrium-constrained problem with f_i and p given by the model formulas, let \gamma\ge1, and suppose hypothesis (H) holds. Let (\bar x,\bar z)\in\widetilde Y_1\times\prod_{i=2}^nY_i, where \bar z is the unique solution of the follower generalized equation at x=\bar x, and set \bar T=\bar x+\sum_{i=2}^n\bar y_i. Suppose that, for each \ell\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\}, either the lower or upper bound on y_{\ell+1} is weakly active and 1-\frac{\bar y_{\ell+1}}{\bar T}\left(\frac1\gamma+1\right)\ne0. Then every i\in\mathbb K(\bar x,\bar z) generates a subgradient of the associated composite objective \Theta at \bar x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the specified Cournot equilibrium-constrained problem, assume γ is at least one, hypothesis (H) holds, and the follower equilibrium at the leader decision is unique. If every follower has a weakly active lower or upper bound and the stated nondegeneracy factor is nonzero, then each index in the set K at the reference solution generates a subgradient of the composite upper-level objective at the leader decision.
assumptions_latex: \text{The functions }f_i\text{ and }p\text{ and the equilibrium-constrained problem are those of the specified model}
\bar z\text{ is the unique solution of the follower generalized equation for }x=\bar x
\forall\ell\in\{1,\ldots,n-1\},\ \text{a lower or upper bound on }y_{\ell+1}\text{ is weakly active}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall i\in\mathbb K(\bar x,\bar z),\quad i\text{ generates an element of }\partial\Theta(\bar x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complementarity-form MPEC and its reformulation boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a generic MPEC and records the MFCQ failure of its standard nonlinear reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complementarity-form MPEC is \(\min_z f(z)\) subject to \(c(z)\ge0\) and \(0\le G(z)\perp H(z)\ge0\). Because \(G(z),H(z)\ge0\), complementarity is equivalent to \(G(z)^T H(z)\le0\). Treating this relation as a standard nonlinear constraint produces an NLP that violates MFCQ at every feasible point. A disjunctive mixed-integer reformulation is also possible, but its relaxations can be weak and lead to large search trees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An MPEC minimizes an objective subject to ordinary constraints and componentwise complementarity constraints. Complementarity can be written as a nonlinear scalar constraint, but the resulting NLP fails MFCQ at every feasible point. A disjunctive mixed-integer representation is possible but may have weak relaxations.
assumptions_latex: z\text{ is feasible for the complementarity-form MPEC}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\le G(z)\perp H(z)\ge0\iff G(z)\ge0,\ H(z)\ge0,\ G(z)^T H(z)\le0,\quad \mathrm{MFCQ}\text{ fails at every feasible point of the resulting NLP}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Face-normal polyhedral decomposition associated with projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covering of the ambient space by face-normal cells and the common-face structure of their intersections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). For the faces \(\mathcal F_I\) of \(P(A,b)\) and their associated cones \(\mathcal N_I\), \[\mathbb{R}^n=\bigcup_{I\in\mathcal I(A,b)}(\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I).\] If distinct \(I,J\in\mathcal I(A,b)\) satisfy \[P_{IJ}:=(\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I)\cap(\mathcal F_J+\mathcal N_J)\neq\varnothing,\] then \[P_{IJ}=(\mathcal F_I\cap\mathcal F_J)+(\mathcal N_I+\mathcal N_J),\] and \(P_{IJ}\) is a common face of \(\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I\) and \(\mathcal F_J+\mathcal N_J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sums of each polyhedral face with its associated normal cone cover the ambient space. Whenever two distinct cells intersect, their intersection is the sum of the face intersection and the two associated normal cones, and is a common face of both cells.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb{R}^n=\bigcup_{I\in\mathcal I(A,b)}(\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I);\quad P_{IJ}\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow P_{IJ}=(\mathcal F_I\cap\mathcal F_J)+(\mathcal N_I+\mathcal N_J)\text{ and }P_{IJ}\text{ is a common face of both cells}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local critical-face reduction for polyhedral projection residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the critical face \(F\) associated with \(y=\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega(x)\) and the residual \(x-y\); the source's face mapping notation \(\mathcal F\) is retained.

Then there exists a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) such that, for every \(x'\in U\), with \(z':=x'-\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega(x')\), \[\mathcal F_\Omega(z')=\mathcal F_F(z').\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near the reference point, the face determined by each projection residual is unchanged when the ambient polyhedral set is replaced by its critical face.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Face geometry and affine projection cells of a polyhedron
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For the inequality representation \(P(A,b)\), indexed faces \(\mathcal F_I\), and their associated cones \(\mathcal N_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\in\mathcal I(A,b)\). Then \[\operatorname{ri}\mathcal F_I=\{x\in\mathcal F_I:A_i\cdot x<b_i\ \forall i\notin I\}.\] For every \(x\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal F_I\), \[\mathcal T(x;P(A,b))=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_i\cdot v\leq0\ \forall i\in I\},\] \[\mathcal N(x;P(A,b))=\operatorname{pos}\{A_{i\cdot}^{T}:i\in I\}=\mathcal N_I,\] and \[\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal F_I-x)=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_i\cdot v=0\ \forall i\in I\}.\] These sets depend only on the face. Moreover, \(\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I\) is full-dimensional. For every \(z\in\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I\), \[\Pi_{P(A,b)}(z)=\Pi_{\mathcal S_I}(z),\qquad \mathcal S_I=\operatorname{aff}\mathcal F_I=\{x:A_{i\cdot}x=b_i\ \forall i\in I\}.\] Hence \(\Pi_{P(A,b)}\) is affine on \(\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I\) and Fréchet differentiable at every interior point of that set. Finally, for every \(x\in\mathcal F_I\), \[\mathcal N_I=\mathcal N(x;P(A,b))\cap\operatorname{aff}\mathcal N_I,\] so \(\mathcal N_I\) is a face of \(\mathcal N(x;P(A,b))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral face has explicit relative-interior, tangent-cone, normal-cone, and direction-space descriptions determined by its active constraints. The face plus its associated normal cone is full-dimensional, and on that region projection onto the polyhedron equals projection onto the face's affine hull. The associated normal cone is also a face of the pointwise normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal F_I\text{ is the face indexed by }I
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ri}\mathcal F_I,\ \mathcal T(x;P(A,b)),\ \mathcal N(x;P(A,b)),\text{ and }\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal F_I-x)\text{ have the stated active-index formulas};\quad \dim\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I)=n;\quad \Pi_{P(A,b)}=\Pi_{\operatorname{aff}\mathcal F_I}\text{ on }\mathcal F_I+\mathcal N_I;\quad \mathcal N_I\text{ is a face of }\mathcal N(x;P(A,b))

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection, critical face, and critical cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records general closed-convex projection properties and defines the critical face and critical cone in the polyhedral specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Its Euclidean projection \(\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega\) is globally Lipschitz with constant \(1\), and \(y=\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega(x)\) if and only if \(x-y\in N_\Omega(y)\). If, additionally, \(\Omega\) is polyhedral and \(y=\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega(x)\), define \[F:=\{c\in\Omega:\langle x-y,c-y\rangle=0\}\] and \[K:=T_\Omega(y)\cap\{x-y\}^{\perp}.\] Then \(F\) is the critical face exposed by \(x-y\), and \(K=T_F(y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a nonempty closed convex set is nonexpansive and is characterized by a normal-cone inclusion. For a polyhedral set, the projection residual exposes a critical face, and the corresponding critical cone equals the tangent cone to that face.
assumptions_latex: \Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}
\Omega\text{ is polyhedral for the critical-face and critical-cone conclusions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Lip}(\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega)\le 1,\quad y=\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega(x)\iff x-y\in N_\Omega(y),\quad F=\{c\in\Omega:\langle x-y,c-y\rangle=0\},\quad K=T_\Omega(y)\cap\{x-y\}^{\perp}=T_F(y).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local critical-cone formula for polyhedral projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact local representation of projection onto a polyhedral set around a reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral, \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(y=\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega(x)\). Let \(K:=T_\Omega(y)\cap\{x-y\}^{\perp}\) be the associated critical cone. Then there exists a neighborhood \(U\) of \(0\) such that, for every \(k\in U\), \[\operatorname{Proj}_\Omega(x+k)=y+\operatorname{Proj}_K(k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally, projection onto a polyhedral set equals the reference projection plus projection of the perturbation onto the associated critical cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni0\ \forall k\in U:\quad \operatorname{Proj}_\Omega(x+k)=y+\operatorname{Proj}_K(k).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projector onto the convex set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection onto a closed convex set in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(z\in\mathbb R^n\), there is a unique point
\[
P_C(z):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\|x-z\|.
\]
For \(x\in C\), the following conditions are equivalent:
\[
x=P_C(z),
\qquad z-x\in N_C(x),
\qquad \langle z-x,y-x\rangle\leq0\quad\text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Moreover, for all \(z,w\in\mathbb R^n\), the projector is firmly nonexpansive:
\[
\|P_Cz-P_Cw\|^2\leq\langle P_Cz-P_Cw,z-w\rangle.
\]
In particular, \(P_C\) is nonexpansive and hence globally Lipschitz with constant one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a closed convex set is unique, firmly nonexpansive, and characterized by the residual belonging to the normal cone.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limiting-Jacobian Inclusion for a Convex-Constraint Projector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generalized-Jacobian relation for the Euclidean projector under constant-rank constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let K be the set specified by the referenced defining relation, with g:\mathcal D\supset K\to\mathbb R^{m} twice continuously differentiable on the open set \mathcal D and every component g_i convex. For x, set \bar x:=\Pi_K(x). If CRCQ holds at \bar x, then
\[
\operatorname{Jac}(\Pi_K'(x;\cdot),0)\supseteq\operatorname{Jac}(\Pi_K,x).
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean Projection onto a Closed Convex Set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closest-point definition and minimization representation of the Euclidean projector; nonemptiness is required for the asserted existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the Euclidean projection of \(x\) onto \(K\) is the unique closest point \[\Pi_K(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in K}\frac12\|y-x\|_2^2.\] The mapping \(\Pi_K:\mathbb{R}^n\to K\) is the Euclidean projector onto \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Euclidean projection onto a nonempty closed convex set is the unique point in the set minimizing squared Euclidean distance to the given point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi_K(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in K}\frac12\|y-x\|_2^2\text{ exists and is unique.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection criterion for constrained best approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness characterized by attainability of the metric projection onto the closed image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\in\mathcal L(\mathcal X,\mathcal Y)\), let \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subseteq\mathcal X\) be closed and convex, and let \(Q_{\mathcal C}\) be the metric projector of \(\mathcal Y\) onto \(\overline{T(\mathcal C)}\). A \(\mathcal C\)-best-approximate solution exists if and only if
\[
Q_{\mathcal C}y\in T(\mathcal C).
\]
Whenever it exists, the \(\mathcal C\)-best-approximate solution is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constrained best-approximate solution exists exactly when the projection of the data onto the closure of the attainable image is itself attainable; the selected solution is then unique.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Piecewise-affine structure of polyhedral projectors and associated VI maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise structure of Euclidean projectors and the natural and normal maps induced by a polyhedral set and a matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedral set. Then \(\Pi_K\) is piecewise affine on \(\mathbb{R}^n\); if \(K\) is a polyhedral cone, \(\Pi_K\) is piecewise linear. Moreover, for every \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), the natural map \[x\mapsto x-\Pi_K(x-Mx)\] and the normal map \[z\mapsto M\Pi_K(z)+z-\Pi_K(z)\] are piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a polyhedral set is piecewise affine, and projection onto a polyhedral cone is piecewise linear. The corresponding natural and normal variational-inequality maps are piecewise affine for every matrix.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fundamental Properties of Euclidean Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, variational characterization, firm nonexpansiveness, nonexpansiveness, and squared-distance smoothness for projection onto a nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Then: (i) \(\Pi_K(x)\) exists uniquely for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\); (ii) \(\bar x=\Pi_K(x)\) if and only if \(\bar x\in K\) and \[(y-\bar x)^T(\bar x-x)\ge0\quad\forall y\in K;\] (iii) for all \(u,v\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \[(\Pi_K(u)-\Pi_K(v))^T(u-v)\ge\|\Pi_K(u)-\Pi_K(v)\|_2^2,\] hence \[\|\Pi_K(u)-\Pi_K(v)\|_2\le\|u-v\|_2;\] and (iv) \[\rho(x):=\frac12\|x-\Pi_K(x)\|_2^2\] is continuously differentiable with \(\nabla\rho(x)=x-\Pi_K(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection onto a nonempty closed convex set exists uniquely, has a variational-inequality characterization, is firmly nonexpansive and therefore nonexpansive, and produces a continuously differentiable squared-distance function whose gradient is the projection residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi_K\text{ is single-valued and firmly nonexpansive, and }\rho(x)=\frac12\|x-\Pi_K(x)\|_2^2\in C^1(\mathbb{R}^n)\text{ with }\nabla\rho(x)=x-\Pi_K(x).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face-indexed normal manifold of a polyhedral convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each nonempty face \(F\in\mathcal F(C)\), let \(N_C(F)\) denote the normal cone \(N_C(x)\) at any \(x\in\operatorname{ri}F\), and define
\[
M_F:=F+N_C(F).
\]
The collection \(\{M_F:F\in\mathcal F(C)\}\) covers \(\mathbb R^n\), and the relative interiors of its full-dimensional cells are pairwise disjoint. If \(z\in M_F\), then \(P_C(z)\in F\); on every cell \(M_F\), the Euclidean projector \(P_C\) agrees with an affine mapping. Thus the face-normal pairs of \(C\) induce a polyhedral subdivision on which projection, and consequently a polyhedral normal map, is piecewise affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each face plus its normal cone forms a normal-manifold cell; these cells cover space and make polyhedral projection piecewise affine.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence, Variational Characterization, and Nonexpansiveness of Convex Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection onto a nonempty closed convex subset of finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be nonempty, closed, and convex. For every z\in\mathbb{R}^n, \Pi_C(z) exists uniquely and is the unique \bar z\in C satisfying (x-\bar z)^T(\bar z-z)\ge 0 for all x\in C. Moreover, for all z,z'\in\mathbb{R}^n, \|\Pi_C(z)-\Pi_C(z')\|_2\le\|z-z'\|_2; hence \Pi_C is globally Lipschitz with constant 1.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint continuity of the Euclidean projector in its input and parameter under the stated convexity, smoothness, and MFCQ assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K(p)\) be the parametric constraint set defined by (4.7.1), and suppose each \(g_i(\cdot,p)\) is convex for every \(p\in\mathcal P\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-selection piecewise map classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For continuous vector-valued maps on a subset of an open Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal O\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open, \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathcal O\), and let \(\Phi:\mathcal O\to\mathbb R^m\) be continuous. For an integer \(k>0\), \(\Phi\) is \(\mathrm{PC}^k\) on \(\mathcal D\) if there are finitely many \(C^k\) maps \(\Phi^1,\ldots,\Phi^I\) on \(\mathcal O\) such that \(\Phi(x)\in\{\Phi^i(x):1\le i\le I\}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal D\). It is piecewise smooth if it is \(\mathrm{PC}^k\) for some \(k>0\), piecewise analytic if the selections can all be analytic, piecewise affine if they can all be affine and \(\mathcal D\) is a finite union of polyhedra, and piecewise linear if the selections can all be linear.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous map is PC-k when, at every point of the specified domain, its value equals the value of one of finitely many C-k selection maps. Requiring suitable finite selections defines piecewise smooth, analytic, affine, and linear maps; the piecewise-affine definition additionally requires the domain to be a finite union of polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The stated finite-selection conditions define the }\mathrm{PC}^k\text{, piecewise-smooth, analytic, affine, and linear classes.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pseudodifferentiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudodifferentiability of a finite-dimensional scalar function at a point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function $z:\mathbb{R}^p\to\mathbb{R}$ is pseudodifferentiable at $x^0$ if there exist an open neighborhood $V$ of $x^0$ and an upper-semicontinuous multifunction $\Gamma_z:V\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^p$ with nonempty compact convex values such that, for $x\in V$ and $g\in\Gamma_z(x)$, $$z(x)=z(x^0)+g(x-x^0)+o(x,x^0,g),$$ and for every sequence $x^k\to x^0$ with $g^k\in\Gamma_z(x^k)$, $$\frac{o(x^k,x^0,g^k)}{\|x^k-x^0\|}\to0.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is pseudodifferentiable at a point when it admits nearby linear models selected from an upper-semicontinuous multifunction with nonempty compact convex values, with an error uniformly little-o along every convergent sequence and every corresponding selection.
assumptions_latex: \Gamma_z:V\rightrightarrows\mathbb{R}^p\text{ is upper semicontinuous with nonempty compact convex values}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z(x)=z(x^0)+g(x-x^0)+o(x,x^0,g),\quad \frac{o(x^k,x^0,g^k)}{\|x^k-x^0\|}\to0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Error-bound transfer across finitely many pieces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A global error bound for a piecewise continuous inequality obtained from selection-wise bounds and linear regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} be piecewise with continuous selections g_i and active sets P^i:=\{x:f(x)=g_i(x)\}. Set S^i:=g_i^{-1}(( -\infty,0]). If each pair (S^i,P^i) is linearly regular and, for every i, there is \eta_i>0 such that \operatorname{dist}(x,S^i)\le \eta_i[g_i(x)]_+ for all x\in\mathbb{R}^n, then there exists \eta>0 such that \operatorname{dist}(x,f^{-1}(( -\infty,0]))\le \eta[f(x)]_+ for all x\in\mathbb{R}^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every continuous selection of a finite piecewise function has a global error bound and its sublevel set is linearly regular with its active region, then the piecewise inequality has a global error bound.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is a finite piecewise continuous function with selections }g_i\text{ and active sets }P^i
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\eta>0\ \forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\quad \operatorname{dist}(x,f^{-1}(( -\infty,0]))\le\eta[f(x)]_+.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent characterizations of an open mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to an arbitrary function from an open Euclidean domain, without continuity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) be open and let \(f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb{R}^m\). The following are equivalent: (i) \(f\) maps every open subset of \(\mathcal D\) to an open subset of \(\mathbb{R}^m\); (ii) for every \(x^\infty\in\mathcal D\) and every sequence \(y^k\to y^\infty=f(x^\infty)\), there exists \(x^k\to x^\infty\) in \(\mathcal D\) such that \(f(x^k)=y^k\) for all sufficiently large \(k\); and (iii) the inverse multifunction \(f^{-1}\) is lower semicontinuous at every graph pair \((y,x)\) with \(x\in\mathcal D\) and \(y=f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function on an open Euclidean domain is open exactly when nearby target sequences can eventually be lifted to source sequences converging to any chosen preimage, equivalently when its inverse multifunction is lower semicontinuous at every graph point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (i)\Longleftrightarrow(ii)\Longleftrightarrow(iii)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuous finite piece-selection function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a general piecewise continuous function without imposing geometric structure beyond closed active sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous function f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} is piecewise if there are continuous functions g_1,\ldots,g_k such that f(x)\in\{g_i(x):1\le i\le k\} for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n. Its active sets P^i:=\{x:f(x)=g_i(x)\} are closed and cover \mathbb{R}^n. Moreover, for any finite family of closed sets S^1,\ldots,S^k, \operatorname{dist}\!\left(x,\bigcup_{i=1}^k S^i\right)=\min_{1\le i\le k}\operatorname{dist}(x,S^i).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous function is piecewise when its value at every point equals one of finitely many continuous selection functions. Each selection's active set is closed, and distance to a finite union of closed sets is the minimum of the distances to its members.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^i=\{x:f(x)=g_i(x)\}\text{ is closed for every }i,\quad \bigcup_{i=1}^kP^i=\mathbb{R}^n,\quad \operatorname{dist}\!\left(x,\bigcup_{i=1}^kS^i\right)=\min_i\operatorname{dist}(x,S^i).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Piecewise linear mappings and extended-real-valued functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional definition using finite polyhedral covers and affine formulas on each piece.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mapping \(F:D\to\mathbb R^m\), where \(D\subset\mathbb R^n\), is piecewise linear on \(D\) if \(D=\bigcup_{k=1}^N D_k\) for finitely many polyhedral sets \(D_k\), and for every \(k\) there exist \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(a_k\in\mathbb R^m\) such that \(F(x)=A_kx+a_k\) for all \(x\in D_k\). A function \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is piecewise linear if its restriction \(f:\operatorname{dom}f\to\mathbb R\) is piecewise linear in this sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mapping is piecewise linear when its domain is a finite union of polyhedral sets and the mapping is affine on each set. An extended-real-valued function is piecewise linear when its finite-valued restriction to its effective domain has this property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F|_{D_k}(x)=A_kx+a_k\ (k=1,\ldots,N);\qquad f\text{ is piecewise linear}\iff f|_{\operatorname{dom}f}:\operatorname{dom}f\to\mathbb R\text{ is piecewise linear}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Determinant-sign criterion for adjacent affine images
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates orientation of two compatible nonsingular affine pieces to the face-to-face geometry of their images.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_1,P_2\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be full-dimensional polyhedra whose intersection is a common \((n-1)\)-dimensional face. Let \(A^1,A^2\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be nonsingular and \(b^1,b^2\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose \(A^1x+b^1=A^2x+b^2\) for every \(x\in P_1\cap P_2\). Then \(A^1P_1+b^1\) and \(A^2P_2+b^2\) intersect in a common \((n-1)\)-dimensional face if and only if \(\det(A^1)\det(A^2)>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two nonsingular affine maps that agree on the common facet of adjacent full-dimensional polyhedra send those polyhedra to sets sharing a common facet exactly when their determinants have the same sign.
assumptions_latex: P_1\cap P_2\text{ is a common }(n-1)\text{-dimensional face of }P_1\text{ and }P_2.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(A^1P_1+b^1\right)\cap\left(A^2P_2+b^2\right)\text{ is a common }(n-1)\text{-face}\iff\det(A^1)\det(A^2)>0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent global topological and orientation conditions for square piecewise-affine maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be piecewise affine. Its inverse is also piecewise affine and has the same properties.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Locally Piecewise Continuously Differentiable Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-selection definition of a PC1 map, including its smooth pieces and active-index set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous map $G:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is $PC^1$ near $x\in\mathcal D$ if there exist an open neighborhood $\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal D$ of $x$, a positive integer $k$, and maps $G^1,\ldots,G^k\in C^1(\mathcal N;\mathbb R^m)$ such that $G(y)\in\{G^1(y),\ldots,G^k(y)\}$ for every $y\in\mathcal N$. Each $G^i$ is a $C^1$ piece of $G$ at $x$, and $\mathcal P(y):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}:G(y)=G^i(y)\}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous map is PC1 near a point if, on an open neighborhood of that point, it selects its value from a finite family of continuously differentiable maps. Those maps are its C1 pieces, and the active-index set records which pieces agree with the map at each argument.
assumptions_latex: G:\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is continuous}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is }PC^1\text{ near }x\iff \exists\,\mathcal N\subseteq\mathcal D,\ k\in\mathbb N_{>0},\ G^1,\ldots,G^k\in C^1(\mathcal N;\mathbb R^m)\text{ such that }\forall y\in\mathcal N,\ G(y)\in\{G^1(y),\ldots,G^k(y)\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Piecewise-C1 Projection onto a Parametric Inequality Set

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the setting of Theorem 4.2.16, let \(\bar v=\bar y-F(\bar x,\bar y)\) and \(C^j(x)=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:g_i(x,y)=0\text{ for }i\in\mathcal I^j\}\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: B-Differentiability of Piecewise-C1 Mappings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local directional differentiability, directional-derivative stability, and piecewise-linear derivative structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G:U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be \(\mathrm{PC}^1\) near \(\bar x\), with \(C^1\) pieces \(G^1,\ldots,G^p\). Then: (a) \(G\) is B-differentiable at every point near \(\bar x\); (b) for every \(\varepsilon>0\) there exists \(\delta>0\) such that \(\|G'(\bar x+h;h)-G'(\bar x;h)\|\le\varepsilon\|h\|\) whenever \(\|h\|<\delta\); and (c) \(G'(\bar x;\cdot)\) is piecewise linear with matrix pieces \(\nabla G^1(\bar x),\ldots,\nabla G^p(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every locally piecewise-C1 map is B-differentiable nearby. Its directional derivative varies to first order continuously in the stated diagonal sense, and the directional-derivative map at the base point is piecewise linear with pieces given by the Jacobians of the smooth selections.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is B-differentiable nearby},\quad \forall\varepsilon>0\ \exists\delta>0\ \forall\|h\|<\delta:\ \|G'(\bar x+h;h)-G'(\bar x;h)\|\le\varepsilon\|h\|,\quad G'(\bar x;\cdot)\text{ is piecewise linear}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the determinant-sign definition and records closure under composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A piecewise-affine map \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is coherently oriented if there exists a finite family of affine pieces \(f^1,\ldots,f^k\) of \(f\) such that \(\det Jf^i\) has the same nonzero sign for every \(i\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent criteria for differentiability of a polyhedral projector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fréchet differentiability characterized through the critical cone and VI nondegeneracy, with additional equivalent conditions when the base point is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedron and \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). The following are equivalent: (a) \(\Pi_K\) is Fréchet differentiable at \(x\); (b) \(\mathcal C_\pi(x;K)\) is a linear subspace; and (c) \(\Pi_K(x)\) is a nondegenerate solution of \(\operatorname{VI}(K,\mathbf I-x)\). If \(x\in K\), these are further equivalent to (b') \(\mathcal T(x;K)\) being a linear subspace and (d) \(0\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal N(x;K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral projector is Fréchet differentiable at a point exactly when its critical cone is a linear subspace, equivalently when the projected point is a nondegenerate solution of the associated variational inequality. If the point lies in the polyhedron, tangent-cone linearity and relative-interior membership of zero in the normal cone are equivalent as well.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pi_K\text{ is F-differentiable at }x\iff \mathcal C_\pi(x;K)\text{ is a linear subspace}\iff \Pi_K(x)\text{ is a nondegenerate solution of }\operatorname{VI}(K,\mathbf I-x);\quad x\in K\Rightarrow\bigl(\text{these}\iff \mathcal T(x;K)\text{ is linear}\iff 0\in\operatorname{ri}\mathcal N(x;K)\bigr)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local critical-cone representation and B-differentiability of a polyhedral projector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local representation and differentiability of Euclidean projection onto a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a polyhedron. For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), there exists a neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(x\) such that, with \(\mathcal C=\mathcal C_\pi(x;K)\), \[\Pi_K(y)=\Pi_K(x)+\Pi_{\mathcal C}(y-x)\qquad\forall y\in\mathcal N.\] Consequently, \[\Pi_K'(x;d)=\Pi_{\mathcal C}(d)\qquad\forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n,\] and \(\Pi_K\) is strongly B-differentiable everywhere on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally around any point, projection onto a polyhedron equals the base projection plus projection of the displacement onto the associated critical cone. Its directional derivative is the critical-cone projector, and it is strongly B-differentiable everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mathcal N\ni x\ \forall y\in\mathcal N:\ \Pi_K(y)=\Pi_K(x)+\Pi_{\mathcal C}(y-x);\quad \Pi_K'(x;d)=\Pi_{\mathcal C}(d)\ \forall d\in\mathbb{R}^n;\quad \Pi_K\text{ is strongly B-differentiable on }\mathbb{R}^n

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the normal map by \(F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=F(P_C(z))+z-P_C(z)\). For polyhedral \(C\) and continuously differentiable \(F\), this map is Bouligand differentiable. Writing \(x=P_C(z)\), the directional chain rule gives \(F_C^{\mathrm{nor}\,'}(z;h)=\nabla F(x)P_C'(z;h)+h-P_C'(z;h)\) for every \(h\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Hence its first-order model combines the smooth Jacobian of \(F\) with the critical-cone projector derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polyhedral normal map is Bouligand differentiable, and its derivative follows by combining the field Jacobian with the projector derivative.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proper Local-Homeomorphism Existence Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general nonlinear-analysis result giving properness, local invertibility, and image-coverage conclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M,N\) be metric spaces, let \(G:M\to N\) be continuous, and let \(M_0\subseteq M\), \(N_0\subseteq N\) satisfy that \(G|_{M_0}\) is a local homeomorphism and \(\varnothing\ne G^{-1}(N_0)\subseteq M_0\). If \(G\) is proper with respect to some \(E\) with \(N_0\subseteq E\subseteq N\), then \(G|_{(G^{-1}(N_0),N_0)}\) is a proper local homeomorphism. If additionally \(N_0\) is connected, then \(G(M_0)\supseteq N_0\) and \(G(\operatorname{cl}M_0)\supseteq E\cap\operatorname{cl}N_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous map that is locally homeomorphic on the relevant domain and proper over a containing target set restricts to a proper local homeomorphism over the target subset. If that subset is connected, the map covers it, and the image of the domain closure covers the portion of its closure lying in the properness set.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is proper with respect to }E
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G|_{(G^{-1}(N_0),N_0)}\text{ is a proper local homeomorphism};\quad N_0\text{ connected}\Rightarrow G(M_0)\supseteq N_0\text{ and }G(\operatorname{cl}M_0)\supseteq E\cap\operatorname{cl}N_0.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha>0\), define \(T_\alpha:K\to K\) by \(T_\alpha(x)=P_K(x-\alpha F(x))\). The map \(T_\alpha\) is continuous and has a fixed point by Brouwer's fixed-point theorem. Moreover, \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}(T_\alpha)\) if and only if \(\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\) for every \(y\in K\). Thus \(\operatorname{Fix}(T_\alpha)=\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The projected field map is continuous, Brouwer guarantees a fixed point, and its fixed-point set is exactly the variational-inequality solution set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(y\in K\), set \(G(y)=\{x\in K:\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\}\). Each \(G(y)\) is closed, and \(G\) has the KKM covering property \(\operatorname{co}\{y_1,\ldots,y_m\}\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^mG(y_i)\). Since \(K\) is compact, the Fan–KKM lemma gives \(x^*\in\bigcap_{y\in K}G(y)\). Therefore \(\langle F(x^*),y-x^*\rangle\geq0\) for every \(y\in K\), so \(x^*\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed-valued KKM correspondence formed from the VI inequalities has nonempty total intersection, and every intersection point solves the VI.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Face reduction and local preimage counts for an LCP normal map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the book's standard LCP normal map $f_M$, face $S_q$, cone $Q_q$, direction set $V_q$, and zero-extension notation $x_\beta^0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $q\in\mathbb R^n$, set $\alpha=\operatorname{supp}q$ and $\beta=\bar\alpha$, and suppose $q\ge0$ and $M_{\beta\beta}$ is nondegenerate. Then (a) for every $x\in S_q$, $(f_M(x))_\alpha=x_\alpha+(f_M(x_\beta^0))_\alpha$ and $(f_M(x))_\beta=f_{M_{\beta\beta}}(x_\beta)$; (b) for every $u\in\operatorname{aff}Q_q$, $v\in V_q$, and $\lambda>0$, $|f_M^{-1}(u+\lambda v)\cap S_q|\le |f_{M_{\beta\beta}}^{-1}(v_\beta)|$; and (c) for every $u\in\operatorname{ri}Q_q$ and $v\in V_q$, there exists $\bar\lambda>0$ such that equality holds in (b) whenever $0<\lambda\le\bar\lambda$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative q whose complementary principal submatrix is nondegenerate, the LCP normal map reduces blockwise on the corresponding face. Its local preimage count is bounded by that of the reduced normal map, and the bound becomes equality for sufficiently small positive perturbations from a relative-interior point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{gathered}\forall x\in S_q:\ (f_M(x))_\alpha=x_\alpha+(f_M(x_\beta^0))_\alpha,\quad(f_M(x))_\beta=f_{M_{\beta\beta}}(x_\beta);\\ \forall u\in\operatorname{aff}Q_q,\forall v\in V_q,\forall\lambda>0:\ |f_M^{-1}(u+\lambda v)\cap S_q|\le|f_{M_{\beta\beta}}^{-1}(v_\beta)|;\\ \forall u\in\operatorname{ri}Q_q,\forall v\in V_q,\exists\bar\lambda>0,\forall\lambda\in(0,\bar\lambda]:\ |f_M^{-1}(u+\lambda v)\cap S_q|=|f_{M_{\beta\beta}}^{-1}(v_\beta)|.\end{gathered}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stability of an isolated local index under first-order-small perturbations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers isolation and local index between continuous maps under the proposition's two local asymptotic conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, bounded, and open, and let \(\Phi,\Upsilon:\operatorname{cl}\Omega\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous. Suppose \(\bar x\in\Omega\) is an isolated \(p\)-point of \(\Phi\), \(\lim_{\bar x\ne x\to\bar x}(\Phi(x)-\Upsilon(x))/\|x-\bar x\|=0\), and \(\liminf_{\bar x\ne x\to\bar x}\|\Upsilon(x)-\Upsilon(\bar x)\|/\|x-\bar x\|>0\). Then \(\bar x\) is an isolated \(p\)-point of \(\Upsilon\), and both indices are well defined and satisfy \(\operatorname{ind}(\Phi,\bar x)=\operatorname{ind}(\Upsilon,\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If two continuous maps differ by a term negligible relative to distance from an isolated target point, while the comparison map separates from its value at least linearly, the point remains an isolated target point and the two local indices agree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\text{ is an isolated }p\text{-point of }\Upsilon,\quad \operatorname{ind}(\Phi,\bar x)\text{ and }\operatorname{ind}(\Upsilon,\bar x)\text{ are well defined, and }\operatorname{ind}(\Phi,\bar x)=\operatorname{ind}(\Upsilon,\bar x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fundamental invariance and calculus properties of topological degree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Collects the proposition's translation, perturbation, boundary, target-component, excision, additivity, and Cartesian-product rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, bounded, and open; let \(\Phi,\Upsilon:\operatorname{cl}\Omega	o\mathbb R^n\) be continuous; and suppose \(p
otin\Phi(\operatorname{bd}\Omega)\). Then \(\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)=\deg(\Phi-p,\Omega)\). If \(\Phi_a(x)=\Phi(x+a)\), then \(\deg(\Phi_a,\Omega-a,p)=\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)\). The degree equals \(\deg(\Upsilon,\Omega,p)\) if \(\max_{x\in\operatorname{cl}\Omega}\|\Phi(x)-\Upsilon(x)\|_\infty<\operatorname{dist}_\infty(p,\Phi(\operatorname{bd}\Omega))\), or if \(\Phi=\Upsilon\) on \(\operatorname{bd}\Omega\). It is unchanged when \(p\) is replaced by \(q\) satisfying \(\|p-q\|_\infty<\operatorname{dist}_\infty(p,\Phi(\operatorname{bd}\Omega))\), and more generally by any \(q\) in the same connected component of \(\mathbb R^n\setminus\Phi(\operatorname{bd}\Omega)\). If \(\Omega_1\subseteq\Omega\) is open and \(p
otin\Phi(\Omega\setminus\Omega_1)\), then \(\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)=\deg(\Phi,\Omega_1,p)\). If \(\Omega=\Omega_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\Omega_2\) with \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\) open, then \(\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)=\deg(\Phi,\Omega_1,p)+\deg(\Phi,\Omega_2,p)\). Finally, if \(\Omega'\subset\mathbb R^m\) is nonempty, bounded, and open, \(\Psi:\operatorname{cl}\Omega'	o\mathbb R^m\) is continuous, and \(q
otin\Psi(\operatorname{bd}\Omega')\), then \(\deg(\Phi	imes\Psi,\Omega	imes\Omega',(p,q))=\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)\deg(\Psi,\Omega',q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topological degree is invariant under target normalization, domain translation, sufficiently small uniform perturbations, boundary-preserving map replacement, and movement of the target within a component of the boundary-image complement. It also satisfies excision, additivity, and a Cartesian-product formula.
assumptions_latex: \varnothing\ne\Omega'\subset\mathbb R^m\text{ is bounded and open, }\Psi:\operatorname{cl}\Omega'\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is continuous, and }q\notin\Psi(\operatorname{bd}\Omega')\text{ for the product rule}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \deg\text{ obeys the stated translation, perturbation, boundary-invariance, target-component, excision, additivity, and product formulas.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Homogeneity of Integer Degree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-scalar homogeneity for a map defined on a cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m be a cone and k\in\mathbb{Z}. A function f:D\to\mathbb{R}^n is positively homogeneous of degree k if, for every t>0 and x\in D, f(tx)=t^k f(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map on a cone is positively homogeneous of integer degree k when scaling its argument by any positive real number t scales its value by t to the power k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall t>0\;\forall x\in D,\quad f(tx)=t^k f(x)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The conclusion compares only target points whose local degrees are well-defined.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard complementary matrices $C_I(\alpha)$ and $C_{\bar M}(\alpha)$ associated with principal pivoting.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Single-Facet Structure Outside \(\mathcal L(M)\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local geometry of the complementary-cone set at a nonexceptional point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $q\in\mathcal K(M)\setminus\mathcal L(M)$. There exist an $(n-1)$-dimensional subspace $H$ and $\delta>0$ such that, for every facet $F$ of every complementary cone relative to $M$, if $B(q,\delta)\cap F\ne\varnothing$, then $B(q,\delta)\cap F=B(q,\delta)\cap H=B(q,\delta)\cap\mathcal K(M)$. For every such $F$, moreover, $H=\operatorname{aff}F$, $\dim F=n-1$, and $q\in\operatorname{ri}F$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a point of K(M) outside L(M), K(M) agrees with one codimension-one subspace. Every complementary-cone facet meeting that neighborhood has this subspace as its affine hull, is n−1 dimensional, and contains q in its relative interior.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is a facet of a complementary cone relative to }M
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B(q,\delta)\cap F=B(q,\delta)\cap H=B(q,\delta)\cap\mathcal K(M),\qquad H=\operatorname{aff}F,\quad \dim F=n-1,\quad q\in\operatorname{ri}F.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nondegenerate Intersection with \(\mathcal K(M)\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally unique, two-sided path crossing of a nonexceptional complementary-cone facet.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, let $q:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n$ be a path, and suppose $q(s)\in\mathcal K(M)$ for some $s\in(0,1)$. The intersection at $q(s)$ is nondegenerate if $q(s)\notin\mathcal L(M)$ and there exist an $(n-1)$-dimensional subspace $H$ and $\delta>0$ such that: (a) the conclusion of the local single-facet theorem holds with $q=q(s)$; (b) for every $t\in(s-\delta,s+\delta)\cap[0,1]$, $q(t)\in H$ implies $t=s$; and (c) each of the two connected components of $B(q(s),\delta)\setminus H$ contains points $q(t)$ for parameters $t$ arbitrarily close to $s$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path crosses K(M) nondegenerately at an interior parameter when the crossing lies outside L(M), K(M) is locally a single facet subspace, the path meets that subspace only at the crossing parameter nearby, and points of the path approach the crossing through both sides.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(s)\notin\mathcal L(M),\quad q(t)\in H\Rightarrow t=s\text{ locally},\quad \forall\eta>0\ \text{each component of }B(q(s),\delta)\setminus H\text{ contains some }q(t)\text{ with }|t-s|<\eta.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common orthant index implies local injectivity and openness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here $S_x$ is the local orthant complex used for the LCP normal map, and the orthant indexes are those of its constituent linear pieces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $q,x\in\mathbb R^n$. Suppose $f_M(x)=q$ and the indexes of every orthant in $S_x$ exist and are identical. Then $f_M$ is injective on $S_x$, and for every $\varepsilon>0$, $f_M(B(x,\varepsilon))$ contains an open ball centered at $q$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all local orthant pieces at a preimage x have defined and identical indexes, the LCP normal map is one-to-one on the local orthant complex and maps every neighborhood of x onto a set containing a neighborhood of q.
assumptions_latex: \text{the indexes of all orthants in }S_x\text{ exist and are identical}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_M|_{S_x}\text{ is injective},\qquad \forall\varepsilon>0,\ \exists\delta>0:\ B(q,\delta)\subseteq f_M(B(x,\varepsilon)).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Endpoint Perturbations Giving Nondegenerate Segment Crossings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic nondegeneracy of intersections along an affine segment path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ and $q,q'\in\mathbb R^n$. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $q''\in B(q',\varepsilon)\setminus\bigl(\mathcal K(M)\cup\{q\}\bigr)$ such that every intersection of $\mathcal K(M)$ with the path of the segment $\ell[q,q'']$ is nondegenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive perturbation radius, the endpoint q′ can be perturbed within that radius, while avoiding K(M) and q, so that every intersection of the resulting segment path with K(M) is nondegenerate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists q''\in B(q',\varepsilon)\setminus\bigl(\mathcal K(M)\cup\{q\}\bigr)\quad\text{such that every intersection of }\mathcal K(M)\text{ with }t\mapsto(1-t)q+tq''\text{ is nondegenerate}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform-perturbation stability of topological degree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The compactness and containment assumptions keep the target away from the boundary image and make the degrees stable for sufficiently large indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R^n be open, let \Phi:\operatorname{cl}\mathcal D\to\mathbb R^n be continuous, and suppose \Phi^{-1}(p) is nonempty and compact. If \Omega is bounded and open, \Phi^{-1}(p)\subseteq\Omega, and \operatorname{cl}\Omega\subseteq\operatorname{cl}\mathcal D, then for every sequence of continuous maps \Phi^k converging uniformly to \Phi on \operatorname{cl}\Omega, \deg(\Phi^k,\Omega,p)=\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p) for all sufficiently large k; hence \deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)=\lim_{k\to\infty}\deg(\Phi^k,\Omega,p).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a continuous map has a nonempty compact inverse image of the target inside a bounded open region, then every uniformly convergent sequence of continuous perturbations has the same degree on that region after finitely many terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists K\;\forall k\ge K:\ \deg(\Phi^k,\Omega,p)=\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p),\quad\text{and thus}\quad \deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)=\lim_{k\to\infty}\deg(\Phi^k,\Omega,p).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree as the sum of local indices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents global degree by the local indices of finitely many target preimages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, bounded, and open, and let \(\Phi:\operatorname{cl}\Omega\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous. If \(p\notin\Phi(\operatorname{bd}\Omega)\) and \(\Phi^{-1}(p)\) is finite, then \[\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)=\sum_{x\in\Phi^{-1}(p)}\operatorname{ind}(\Phi,x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the target is avoided on the boundary and has finitely many preimages, the global degree equals the sum of the local indices at those preimages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)=\sum_{x\in\Phi^{-1}(p)}\operatorname{ind}(\Phi,x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: LCP Complementary-Vertex Polytope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the normalized feasible polytope associated with a square matrix and the notion of an index-complementary vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), define \[\mathcal P_M:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x\ge0,\;Mx\ge0,\;e^{\mathrm T}x=1\}.\] Then \(\mathcal P_M\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x\ge0,\ e^{\mathrm T}x=1\}\). A vertex \(x\) of \(\mathcal P_M\) is \(\bar\imath\)-complementary if \(x_j(Mx)_j=0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\{i\}\); it may be called complementary when the exceptional index is left implicit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a square matrix M, P_M consists of normalized nonnegative vectors x for which Mx is nonnegative. It lies in the standard (n−1)-simplex. A vertex is i-bar-complementary when x_j(Mx)_j = 0 at every index except possibly i; the index may be omitted when understood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P_M=\{x\ge0:Mx\ge0,\ e^{\mathrm T}x=1\},\quad x\text{ is }\bar\imath\text{-complementary}\iff \forall j\ne i,\ x_j(Mx)_j=0

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Axiomatic definition of topological degree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines integer-valued topological degree on the source's admissible collection of triples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An integer-valued function \(\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)\) on triples \((\Phi,\Omega,p)\in\Gamma\) is a topological degree if: (A1) \(\deg(I,\Omega,p)=1\) whenever \(p\in\Omega\); (A2) if \(\Omega_1,\Omega_2\subseteq\Omega\) are disjoint and open and \(p\notin\Phi(\operatorname{cl}\Omega\setminus(\Omega_1\cup\Omega_2))\), then \(\deg(\Phi,\Omega,p)=\deg(\Phi,\Omega_1,p)+\deg(\Phi,\Omega_2,p)\); and (A3) for continuous \(H:\operatorname{cl}\Omega\times[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n\) and \(p:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(p(t)\notin H(\operatorname{bd}\Omega,t)\) for all \(t\in[0,1]\), the value \(\deg(H(\cdot,t),\Omega,p(t))\) is independent of \(t\). The notation \(\deg(\Phi,\Omega)\) abbreviates \(\deg(\Phi,\Omega,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topological degree is an integer-valued invariant characterized by normalization, additivity over separated regions containing all relevant preimages, and invariance under boundary-avoiding homotopies. Omitting the target denotes target zero.
assumptions_latex: \Omega_1,\Omega_2\subseteq\Omega\text{ are disjoint and open in the additivity axiom}
H:\operatorname{cl}\Omega\times[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n\text{ and }p:[0,1]\to\mathbb R^n\text{ are continuous in the homotopy axiom}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \deg\text{ satisfies normalization, additivity, and boundary-avoiding homotopy invariance.}
