knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed parameter range and continuous response quantities for structured strongly monotone VIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary perturbation-response properties for polyhedral VIs generated by a continuous strongly monotone composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}, let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be polyhedral, and let G:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^m be continuous and strongly monotone on \operatorname{range}(A). Then there exist \eta_1,\eta_2>0 such that, for every b\in\mathcal{R}(K,G,A), a solution x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,G,A) exists with \|x\|\leq\eta_1(\|b\|+\|v(b)\|)+\eta_2. Moreover, \mathcal{R}(K,G,A) is closed, and for b\in\mathcal{R}(K,G,A), v(b')\to v(b) and w(b')\to w(b) as b'\to b relative to \mathcal{R}(K,G,A).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There are parameter-independent positive constants giving the stated solution-norm estimate for every admissible parameter. The admissible parameter set is closed, and the response quantities v and w are continuous relative to that set.
assumptions_latex: G:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^m\text{ is continuous and strongly monotone on }\operatorname{range}(A)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\eta_1,\eta_2>0\;\forall b\in\mathcal{R}(K,G,A)\;\exists x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,G,A):\ \|x\|\leq\eta_1(\|b\|+\|v(b)\|)+\eta_2;\quad \mathcal{R}(K,G,A)\text{ is closed};\quad \lim_{\substack{b'\in\mathcal{R}(K,G,A)\\b'\to b}}v(b')=v(b),\ \lim_{\substack{b'\in\mathcal{R}(K,G,A)\\b'\to b}}w(b')=w(b).

knowledge_statements.title: KKT-Triple Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local residual bound for smooth inequality-and-equality constrained VI KKT systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=(x,\lambda,\mu)\), define \[R_{\rm KKT}(z)=\bigl(F(x)+\nabla g(x)^\top\lambda+\nabla h(x)^\top\mu,\ h(x),\ \min\{\lambda,-g(x)\}\bigr),\] where the minimum is componentwise, and let \(Z^*=\{z:\lambda\geq0,\ R_{\rm KKT}(z)=0\}\). A local KKT-triple error bound at \(\bar z\in Z^*\) holds if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\leq\kappa\|R_{\rm KKT}(z)\|\] whenever \(\lambda\geq0\) and \(\|z-\bar z\|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a reference KKT triple, a KKT-triple error bound controls distance to the KKT-triple set by the stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity residual.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) are continuously differentiable.
\((\bar x,\bar\lambda,\bar\mu)\) is a KKT triple with \(\bar\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A KKT-triple error bound is \(\operatorname{dist}(z,Z^*)\leq\kappa\|R_{\rm KKT}(z)\|\) locally around \(\bar z\).

knowledge_statements.title: Linearly Constrained Composite-VI Error Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized-equation error bound for a convex composite VI over linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=(x,\lambda)\), define \[H(z)=\bigl(F(x)+\partial g(x)+A^\top\lambda,\ b-Ax+N_{\mathbb R_+^m}(\lambda)\bigr).\] The inclusion \(0\in H(z)\) represents the composite VI condition \(0\in F(x)+\partial g(x)+N_C(x)\) together with a compatible multiplier. If \(H\) is metrically subregular at \((\bar z,0)\), then there exist \(\kappa>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(z,H^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,H(z))\] whenever \(\|z-\bar z\|<\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity of the composite primal-dual KKT mapping bounds local solution distance by its stationarity and linear-complementarity residual.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Metric subregularity of \(H\) at \((\bar z,0)\) yields \(\operatorname{dist}(z,H^{-1}(0))\leq\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,H(z))\) locally.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Representation-Based Linear Metric Regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines both representation-dependent and intrinsic distance-based linear metric regularity for a finite family of sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For S_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\le0\}, i=1,\ldots,k, and S=\bigcap_{i=1}^kS_i, the family is linearly metrically regular with respect to these representations if there exists c>0 such that \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\max_{1\le i\le k}(g_i(x))_+ for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n. If g_i(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,S_i) for every i, the family \{S_i\} is called linearly metrically regular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite represented set family is linearly metrically regular when distance to its intersection is globally bounded by a constant times the largest positive constraint violation. Using each individual set distance as its representation gives intrinsic linear metric regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c>0\ \forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\max_{1\le i\le k}(g_i(x))_+

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of a Global Convex Inequality Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The boundary condition is retained in normalized conic-subgradient form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\le0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\ne\varnothing, where the g_i are convex, and fix \eta>0. Then \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\eta\max_{1\le i\le m}(g_i(x))_+ for every x\in\mathbb{R}^n if and only if nondifferentiable Abadie CQ holds at every point of S and \inf_{\bar x\in\partial S}\inf_{\substack{\lambda\ge0,\ w^j\in\partial g_j(\bar x)\\\|\sum_{j\in\mathcal I(\bar x)}\lambda_jw^j\|=1}}\max_{i\in\mathcal I(\bar x)}\max_{v\in\partial g_i(\bar x)}v^T\sum_{j\in\mathcal I(\bar x)}\lambda_jw^j\ge\eta^{-1}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty convex inequality system, a global distance bound with constant η is equivalent to Abadie CQ holding everywhere on the feasible set together with a uniform boundary separation condition of at least 1/η for normalized conic combinations of active subgradients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ \operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\eta\max_i(g_i(x))_+\bigr]\iff\bigl[\text{Abadie CQ holds on }S\text{ and the stated boundary infimum is at least }\eta^{-1}\bigr]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal Cones to Two Linearly Metrically Regular Convex Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The first conclusion uses representation-based regularity; the second uses the distance representations defining intrinsic regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S_i=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:g_i(x)\le0\}, i=1,2, where S_i are closed and convex and g_i are real-valued convex functions, and set S=S_1\cap S_2. If the pair is linearly metrically regular with respect to these representations, then every \bar x\in S satisfying g_1(\bar x)=g_2(\bar x)=0 obeys \mathcal N(\bar x;S)=\mathbb R_+\partial g_1(\bar x)+\mathbb R_+\partial g_2(\bar x). If the pair is intrinsically linearly metrically regular, then \mathcal N(\bar x;S)=\mathcal N(\bar x;S_1)+\mathcal N(\bar x;S_2).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two closed convex inequality sets, linear metric regularity gives an exact normal-cone intersection formula. With general convex representations the normal cone is the sum of conic subdifferentials; with distance representations it is the sum of the individual normal cones.
assumptions_latex: S_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is closed and convex},\quad i=1,2
\{S_1,S_2\}\text{ is linearly metrically regular with respect to the stated representations}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local natural-residual error bound for structured strongly monotone VIs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-pointwise local error bound for a polyhedral variational inequality with a composite operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}, let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be polyhedral, and let G:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^m be strongly monotone and Lipschitz continuous on \operatorname{range}(A). For b\in\mathcal{R}(K,G,A), define F(x)=A^TG(Ax)+b. knowledge_statements.statement_title: R-zero criterion for a local natural-residual VI error bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A multiplier-wise sufficient criterion, with a converse under isolation and CRCQ or uniqueness of the extended multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K be a finitely representable convex set of the stated form, where h is affine and every g_i is convex and twice continuously differentiable. Let F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be continuously differentiable, and let x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F) satisfy SBCQ. If, for every (\mu,\lambda)\in\mathcal M^e(x^*), the pair \bigl(\mathcal C,J_x\mathbf L(x^*,\lambda)\bigr) is an R_0 pair, then \operatorname{SOL}(K,F) has a Lipschitzian error bound near x^* with residual \|\mathbf F_K^{\mathrm{nat}}(x)\|. Conversely, if x^* is isolated and either CRCQ holds or \mathcal M^e(x^*) is a singleton, then that error bound implies the R_0 condition for every (\mu,\lambda)\in\mathcal M^e(x^*).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an SBCQ solution of a smoothly represented convex VI, the multiplier-wise R-zero condition implies a local natural-residual error bound. For an isolated solution, the converse requires CRCQ or a unique extended multiplier.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ has the stated finite convex representation with }h\text{ affine and each }g_i\in C^2
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall(\mu,\lambda)\in\mathcal M^e(x^*),\ (\mathcal C,J_x\mathbf L(x^*,\lambda))\text{ is an }R_0\text{ pair}\bigr]\Rightarrow\text{the stated local error bound};\quad\text{the converse holds if }x^*\text{ is isolated and }\bigl(\mathrm{CRCQ}\text{ holds or }\mathcal M^e(x^*)\text{ is a singleton}\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact-domain globalization of a local natural-residual error bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local-to-global result for VI solution-set error bounds, including its compact-polyhedral AVI consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be compact and convex, let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous, and let \(S=\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\). If \(S\) admits a local Lipschitzian error bound with the natural residual, then \(S\) admits a global Lipschitzian error bound with the same residual. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stability and Residual Bounds for Uniform-P Parametric NCPs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of compact parameterization, the uniform P property, and joint Lipschitz continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be compact, suppose $F$ satisfies UNI-P and LIP, and let $y(x)$ denote the NCP solution. Then: (a) for every $\delta>0$, $$L_\delta=\{(x,y)\in X\times\mathbb{R}_+^m:y^TF(x,y)\le\delta,\ F(x,y)\ge0\}$$ is compact; (b) $y(\cdot)$ is Lipschitz continuous on $X$; (c) there exists $\tau>0$ such that $$\lVert y-y(x)\rVert\le\tau\lVert\min\{y,F(x,y)\}\rVert$$ for every $(x,y)\in X\times\mathbb{R}_+^m$; and (d) for every $\delta>0$ there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every $(x,y)\in X\times\mathbb{R}_+^m$, $$\bigl[\lVert\min\{y,F(x,y)\}\rVert\ge\delta\ \lor\ y^TF(x,y)\ge\delta\bigr]\Longrightarrow\lVert y-y(x)\rVert\ge\varepsilon.$$ Here the minimum is componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness, the uniform P property, and joint Lipschitz continuity, the complementarity level sets are compact, the NCP solution is Lipschitz in the parameter, distance to that solution is globally bounded by the minimum-function residual, and a residual or complementarity product bounded away from zero forces a positive distance from the solution.
assumptions_latex: y(x)\text{ denotes the parameterized NCP solution}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\forall\delta>0,\ L_\delta\text{ is compact})\land(y(\cdot)\text{ is Lipschitz on }X)\land(\exists\tau>0\ \forall(x,y)\in X\times\mathbb{R}_+^m:\ \lVert y-y(x)\rVert\le\tau\lVert\min\{y,F(x,y)\}\rVert)\land(\forall\delta>0\ \exists\varepsilon>0\ \forall(x,y)\in X\times\mathbb{R}_+^m:\ [\lVert\min\{y,F(x,y)\}\rVert\ge\delta\lor y^TF(x,y)\ge\delta]\Rightarrow\lVert y-y(x)\rVert\ge\varepsilon)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Complementarity-Product Error Bound for a Parametric NCP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global distance bound under uniform P, Lipschitz, and nondegeneracy assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be compact. Suppose $F$ satisfies UNI-P and LIP and, for every $x\in X$, the NCP solution $y(x)$ is nondegenerate, $$y(x)+F(x,y(x))>0$$ componentwise. Let $S$ be the set defined in (28). Then there exists $\tau>0$ such that $$\operatorname{dist}((x,y),S)\le\tau y^TF(x,y)$$ for every $(x,y)\in X\times\mathbb{R}_+^m$ satisfying $F(x,y)\ge0$.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine VI global error bounds and Lipschitz solution maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between a uniform projection-residual error bound and global Lipschitz stability for affine variational inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and convex and M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}. The following are equivalent: (i) there exists c>0 such that, for every q\in\mathcal{R}(K,M) and x\in\mathbb{R}^n, \[\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M))\le c\|x-\Pi_K(x-q-Mx)\|;\] (ii) (K,M) is a Lipschitzian pair, meaning that some c'>0 satisfies, for all q,q'\in\mathcal{R}(K,M), \[\operatorname{SOL}(K,q',M)\subseteq\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)+c'\|q-q'\|\,\operatorname{cl}\mathbb{B}.\] If K is polyhedral and \mathcal{R}(K,M)=\mathbb{R}^n, these conditions are also equivalent to \operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M) being a singleton for every q\in\mathbb{R}^n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an affine variational inequality over a closed convex set, a uniform global error bound in terms of the projection residual is equivalent to global Lipschitz stability of its solution map. If the set is polyhedral and every right-hand side is solvable, both are further equivalent to unique solvability for every right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ is polyhedral and }\mathcal{R}(K,M)=\mathbb{R}^n\text{ for the singleton equivalence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Uniform projection-residual error bound}\iff\text{Lipschitzian pair};\quad K\text{ polyhedral and }\mathcal{R}(K,M)=\mathbb{R}^n\implies\bigl(\text{these}\iff\forall q\in\mathbb{R}^n,\ |\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)|=1\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Residual Domination by the Complementarity Product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform residual comparison on a prescribed residual-bounded region under nondegeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be compact. Suppose $F$ satisfies UNI-P and LIP and, for every $x\in X$, the NCP solution $y(x)$ is nondegenerate: $$y(x)+F(x,y(x))>0$$ componentwise. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient-Residual Domination Implies a Global Hölder Error Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth minimization over a closed convex set under a global constrained-gradient domination inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable on an open set \(\mathcal D\supseteq S\) and bounded below on \(S\). Set \(f_{\inf}=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\). Suppose \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), \(\delta>0\), and, whenever \(x\in S\) and \(f(x)>f_{\inf}\), \(\operatorname{dist}(-\nabla f(x),\mathcal N(x;S))\ge\delta(f(x)-f_{\inf})^{1-\gamma}\). Then: (a) for every sequence \(\{x^k\}\subset S\), convergence of this residual to zero implies \(f(x^k)\to f_{\inf}\); (b) \(S_{\mathrm{opt}}=\{x\in S:f(x)=f_{\inf}\}\) is nonempty; and (c) \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S_{\mathrm{opt}})\le(\gamma\delta)^{-1}(f(x)-f_{\inf})^\gamma\) for every \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global lower bound on the constrained gradient residual by a power of the objective gap ensures asymptotic objective optimality of residual-vanishing sequences, attainment of the infimum, and a global Hölder error bound.
assumptions_latex: S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is closed and convex}
f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R\text{ is continuously differentiable and bounded below on }S
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[\operatorname{dist}(-\nabla f(x^k),\mathcal N(x^k;S))\to0\Rightarrow f(x^k)\to f_{\inf}\right],\quad S_{\mathrm{opt}}\ne\varnothing,\quad \operatorname{dist}(x,S_{\mathrm{opt}})\le\frac{(f(x)-f_{\inf})^\gamma}{\gamma\delta}\ \forall x\in S

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ekeland Variational Principle in Finite Dimensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate minimizers of continuous, bounded-below functions on closed Euclidean sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed, and let \(f\) be continuous on a set containing \(S\) and bounded below on \(S\). If \(u\in S\), \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), and \(f(u)\le \inf_{x\in S}f(x)+\varepsilon\), then for every \(\delta>0\) there exists \(\bar x\in S\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathbb B(u,\varepsilon/\delta)\) such that \(f(\bar x)\le f(u)\) and \(f(y)+\delta\|\bar x-y\|>f(\bar x)\) for every \(y\in S\setminus\{\bar x\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every delta greater than zero, an epsilon-minimizer can be replaced by a no-worse point within distance epsilon over delta that is a strict minimizer of the function perturbed by delta times distance from that point.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar x\in S\cap\operatorname{cl}\mathbb B(u,\varepsilon/\delta):\ f(\bar x)\le f(u)\ \land\ \forall y\in S\setminus\{\bar x\},\ f(y)+\delta\|\bar x-y\|>f(\bar x)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: R0 criterion for global natural-residual bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates the R0 property of a polyhedral affine-VI pair to global Lipschitzian natural-residual error bounds over all solvable right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be polyhedral and \(M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). If \((K,M)\) is an \(R_0\) pair, then for every \(q\in\mathcal R(K,M)\), a global Lipschitzian error bound for \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)\) holds in terms of the natural residual of \((K,q,M)\). Conversely, if this bound holds for every \(q\in\mathcal R(K,M)\) and there exists \(\bar q\in\mathcal R(K,M)\) such that \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,\bar q,M)\) is bounded, then \((K,M)\) is an \(R_0\) pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The R0 property guarantees a global natural-residual error bound for every solvable right-hand side. The converse requires the additional existence of a solvable right-hand side with a bounded solution set.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone VI Global Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-sharpness global bound for a finite-dimensional monotone VI using the primal gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(G(x)=\sup_{y\in K}\langle F(x),x-y\rangle\) and let \(S\) be the VI solution set. If there exists \(\alpha>0\) such that \(\langle F(x^*),x-x^*\rangle\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\) for every \(x\in K\) and every \(x^*\in P_S(x)\), then \[\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\frac{G(x)}{\alpha}\qquad\text{for every }x\in K.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous monotone VI satisfying the stated weak-sharpness condition, the primal gap globally bounds distance to the solution set with constant one over the sharpness modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:K\to\mathbb R^n\) is continuous and monotone.
The VI solution set \(S\) is nonempty, and the primal gap \(G(x)\) is finite for every \(x\in K\).
For some \(\alpha>0\), every \(x\in K\) and every \(x^*\in P_S(x)\) satisfy \(\langle F(x^*),x-x^*\rangle\geq\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in K\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq G(x)/\alpha\).

knowledge_statements.title: Affine VI Global Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that affinity and polyhedral feasibility alone do not ensure a global natural-residual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine VI on \(K=\mathbb R_+\) with \(F(x)=1\) has solution set \(S=\{0\}\) and natural residual \[r(x)=x-P_K(x-1)=\begin{cases}x,&0\leq x\leq1,\\1,&x\geq1.\end{cases}\] Hence \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)=x\) while \(|r(x)|=1\) for \(x\geq1\), and no finite \(\kappa\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa|r(x)|\) for every \(x\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant affine monotone VI on a polyhedral set can have bounded natural residual while distance to its solution set grows without bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite \(\kappa\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\leq\kappa|r(x)|\) for every \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Well-Behaved and Strongly Well-Behaved Optimization Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic and quantitative constrained-gradient residual conditions for smooth minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, let \(f\) be continuously differentiable on an open set containing \(S\) and bounded below on \(S\), and set \(f_{\inf}=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\). It is strongly well-behaved if there exist \(\delta>0\) and \(\gamma\in(0,1]\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(-\nabla f(x),\mathcal N(x;S))\ge\delta(f(x)-f_{\inf})^{1-\gamma}\) for every \(x\in S\) with \(f(x)>f_{\inf}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pair is well-behaved when every feasible sequence with vanishing constrained-gradient residual approaches the infimum in objective value. It is strongly well-behaved when that residual globally dominates a power of the objective gap.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact-set global bound for a subanalytic VI residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be compact and let \(r:U\to[0,\infty)\) be continuous and subanalytic on an open neighborhood \(U\) of \(K\). If \(S:=\{x\in K:r(x)=0\}\) is nonempty, then there exist constants \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in(0,1]\) such that
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\,r(x)^\theta\qquad\text{for every }x\in K.
\]
Thus an analytic or subanalytic VI formulation has a Hölder global error bound on each compact region where its chosen nonnegative residual has exactly the solution set as its zero set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous subanalytic residual controls distance to its zero set by a Hölder power uniformly on any fixed compact region.
knowledge_statements.title: Analytic-Problem Global Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The compact-set Hölder bound is mathematically plausible as a subanalytic Łojasiewicz-type error bound and fits the theorem container, but no source is supplied for the required hypotheses or exponent conclusion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification by convergent multipliers under strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose constraints are represented near \(\bar x\) by \(g_i(x)\le0\), and a primal-multiplier sequence satisfies \((x^k,\lambda^k)\to(\bar x,\bar\lambda)\). Assume strict complementarity in the form
\[
\bar\lambda_i>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g_i(\bar x)=0.
\]
For any threshold \(\tau\) satisfying \(0<\tau<\min_{i\in A(\bar x)}\bar\lambda_i\), define \(A_k(\tau):=\{i:\lambda_i^k>\tau\}\). Then there exists \(k_0\) such that \(A_k(\tau)=A(\bar x)\) for every \(k\ge k_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent multipliers identify the exact active constraints after finitely many iterations when strict complementarity holds.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\) if and only if \(0\in F(x)+\rho\,\partial d_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise exact distance penalization at feasible VI candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be nonempty, closed, and convex in a Hilbert space \(H\), and let \(d_C\) denote distance to \(C\). For any \(x\in C\) and any \(\rho\ge\|F(x)\|\),
\[
\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for all }y\in C
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0\in F(x)+\rho\,\partial d_C(x).
\]
Accordingly, the nonsmooth distance term is exact at every feasible candidate once the penalty parameter dominates the norm of the VI operator there. The assertion is pointwise and does not claim that every stationary point of the unconstrained penalized inclusion is feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible point, a distance penalty reproduces the VI condition once its parameter dominates the operator norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Penalization for VIs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pointwise equivalence follows from the feasible-point formula for the convex subdifferential of the distance function and is appropriately limited to feasible candidates, but the record supplies no supporting citation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Here (5.1) is the variational inequality on K, and C(x) is the source-defined cone at x.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose F is monotone on K. Then x\in K solves (5.1) if and only if \langle F(y),y-x\rangle\ge 0 for every y\in K. knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a Hilbert space \(H\), with metric projection \(P_C\), and let \(F:H\to H\). The natural residual of the variational inequality is
\[
R_N(x):=x-P_C\bigl(x-F(x)\bigr),\qquad x\in H.
\]
Its norm is a computable stationarity measure. In particular,
\[
R_N(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in C\ \text{ and }\ \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The natural residual is the displacement from a point to its projected forward step, and it vanishes exactly at VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Natural Residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Natural-map degree and solution properties for an R0 cone–matrix pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a closed convex cone and $M\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, with $(K,M)$ an $R_0$ pair. Assume either (A) $M$ is copositive on $K$, or (B) there exists $q^*\in\operatorname{int}K^*$ such that $\operatorname{SOL}(K,q^*,M)=\{0\}$. Then, for every $q\in\mathbb R^n$, $\operatorname{SOL}(K,q,M)$ is nonempty and bounded. assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a Hilbert space \(H\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter II. Variational Inequalities in Hilbert Space p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\) in a Hilbert space \(H\), a map \(F:H\to H\), and a fixed scale \(\alpha>0\), define
\[
R_\alpha(x):=x-P_C\bigl(x-\alpha F(x)\bigr).
\]
The projection optimality condition gives the scale-independent zero-set identity
\[
R_\alpha(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in C\ \text{ and }\ \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Thus changing a fixed positive scale changes residual magnitudes but not the certified VI solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every fixed positive projection scale yields the same residual zero set, although residual magnitudes depend on the scale.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Projection Residuals

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(H(x)\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(P_C^{H(x)}\) denote projection onto \(C\) in the norm induced by \(H(x)\). Define
\[
R_H(x):=x-P_C^{H(x)}\bigl(x-H(x)^{-1}F(x)\bigr).
\]
Then
\[
R_H(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in C\ \text{ and }\ \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Pointwise positive definiteness is sufficient for this zero-set equivalence; uniform metric bounds are needed only for uniform norm comparisons and error estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite point-dependent metric preserves the VI residual zero set, though uniform estimates require stronger metric control.

assumptions_latex: Variable metrics are symmetric positive definite but lack a uniform upper spectral bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No constant \(c\) uniformly satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\|R_{H_k}(x)\|\) for all metrics in the family.

notation.meaning: Solution set of the example VI.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform error bounds when metric spectra are unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Pointwise positive definiteness does not ensure metric-uniform residual bounds. Consider \(C=\mathbb{R}\), \(F(x)=x\), and \(H_k=kI\). The VI solution set is \(S=\{0\}\), while the variable-metric projection residual is
\[
R_{H_k}(x)=x-P_C^{H_k}\bigl(x-H_k^{-1}F(x)\bigr)=\frac{x}{k}.
\]
At \(x=1\), one has \(\operatorname{dist}(1,S)=1\) but \(\lvert R_{H_k}(1)\rvert=1/k\to0\). Hence no metric-independent constant \(c\) can satisfy \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le c\lVert R_{H_k}(x)\rVert\) throughout this family. A uniform upper spectral bound is therefore necessary for such a comparison in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unbounded metric eigenvalues can drive residuals to zero away from the solution set, destroying metric-uniform error bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Variation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally correct and the failure_boundary kind exactly fits the leaf, but the record has no source for the general metric-variation boundary claim.

assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex in a Hilbert space \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=0\) if and only if \(P_C(z)\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(F,C)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-map equation associated with a closed convex VI.

source_refs.locator: Chapter II. Variational Inequalities in Hilbert Space p. 23

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P_C\) be the metric projection onto a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subset H\). For \(z\in H\), set \(x(z):=P_C(z)\) and define the normal map
\[
F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z):=F\bigl(x(z)\bigr)+z-x(z).
\]
Then
\[
F_C^{\mathrm{nor}}(z)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x(z)\in C\ \text{ and }\ \langle F(x(z)),y-x(z)\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
Thus a zero of the unconstrained normal-map residual projects to a VI solution; conversely, every VI solution \(x\) is obtained from \(z=x-F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal map converts the VI into an unconstrained equation whose zeros project exactly to VI solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Map Residual

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varphi:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(F:H\to H\), and fix \(\gamma>0\). Define
\[
R_\gamma^{\mathrm{prox}}(x):=\gamma^{-1}\left[x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\varphi}\bigl(x-\gamma F(x)\bigr)\right].
\]
Then
\[
R_\gamma^{\mathrm{prox}}(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0\in F(x)+\partial\varphi(x).
\]
When \(\varphi\) is the indicator of a closed convex set \(C\), the proximal mapping becomes \(P_C\), so this residual reduces to the scaled projection residual divided by \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A forward-proximal displacement vanishes exactly at solutions of the generalized VI involving a convex subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_\gamma^A(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in F(x)+A(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, let \(F:H\to H\), and fix \(\gamma>0\). With resolvent \(J_{\gamma A}:=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\), define
\[
R_\gamma^A(x):=\gamma^{-1}\left[x-J_{\gamma A}\bigl(x-\gamma F(x)\bigr)\right].
\]
The resolvent is everywhere single-valued, and
\[
R_\gamma^A(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
0\in F(x)+A(x).
\]
Hence the residual norm supplies a fixed-point certificate for the monotone inclusion representing the generalized variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The forward-resolvent displacement is zero exactly when the associated maximal-monotone inclusion is satisfied.

children.title: Proximal–Resolvent Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between proximal and resolvent residual forms.

assumptions_latex: \(\varphi:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\varphi}=J_{\gamma\partial\varphi}\) and \(R_\gamma^{\mathrm{prox}}=R_\gamma^{\partial\varphi}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex proximal maps as subdifferential resolvents.

source_refs.locator: Chapter III. Variational Inequalities for Monotone Operators p. 83
source_refs.source_title: An Introduction to Variational Inequalities and Their Applications

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every proper lower-semicontinuous convex function \(\varphi:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and every \(\gamma>0\), its subdifferential is maximal monotone and
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\varphi}=(I+\gamma\partial\varphi)^{-1}=J_{\gamma\partial\varphi}.
\]
Consequently, for any single-valued map \(F:H\to H\),
\[
R_\gamma^{\mathrm{prox}}(x)=\gamma^{-1}\left[x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\varphi}(x-\gamma F(x))\right]
=R_\gamma^{\partial\varphi}(x).
\]
Thus the proximal and resolvent residual formulations are identical when the monotone operator is a convex subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(C=\mathbb{R}_+^n\), the variational inequality for \(F\) is equivalent to
\[
x\ge0,\qquad F(x)\ge0,\qquad x_iF_i(x)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
It is also equivalent to the natural-residual equation
\[
x-[x-F(x)]_+=0.
\]
Define \(\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(a,b):=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}-a-b\) and \((\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x))_i:=\phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x_i,F_i(x))\). Then
\[
\Phi_{\mathrm{FB}}(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\text{ solves }\operatorname{VI}(F,\mathbb{R}_+^n).
\]
These equations provide the residual interface between VI and complementarity formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the nonnegative orthant, VI solutions are exactly complementarity solutions and zeros of projection or Fischer–Burmeister residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Complementarity Residual Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Lipschitz error bound for a generalized equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a local error-bound property of a gap function near an MPEC solution; such a bound can support exact penalization and optimality analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(\widehat{x},\widehat{z})$ be a local MPEC solution, let $\mathcal E$ be the solution set of the associated generalized equation, and let $G$ be a gap function. The function $G$ is a local Lipschitz error bound near $(\widehat{x},\widehat{z})$ if there exist a neighborhood $\mathcal O$ of $(\widehat{x},\widehat{z})$ and $\gamma>0$ such that $\operatorname{dist}_{\mathcal E}(x,z)\leq\gamma\lVert G(x,z)\rVert$ for every $(x,z)\in\mathcal O$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A gap function is a local Lipschitz error bound near a local MPEC solution when, throughout some neighborhood, the distance to the generalized-equation solution set is bounded by a positive constant times the norm of the gap.
assumptions_latex: (\widehat{x},\widehat{z})\text{ is a local solution of the MPEC}
G\text{ is a gap function for the associated generalized equation}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall (x,z)\in\mathcal O,\quad \operatorname{dist}_{\mathcal E}(x,z)\leq\gamma\lVert G(x,z)\rVert.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit complementarity problem and minimum-residual reformulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specializes a GQVI with a translated nonnegative orthant and derives equivalent complementarity and minimum-residual formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
K(x)=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:y\geq m(x)\},
\]
where \(m:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(\Phi:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be single-valued. Then \(\operatorname{GQVI}(K,\Phi)\) is equivalent to
\[
0\leq x-m(x)\perp\Phi(x)\geq0.
\]
For \(c>0\) and \(x\geq m(x)\), the associated regularized gap satisfies
\[
\theta_c(x)\geq\frac c2\left\|\min\left\{x-m(x),c^{-1}\Phi(x)\right\}\right\|^2
\]
and
\[
\theta_c(x)=0\iff\min\left\{x-m(x),c^{-1}\Phi(x)\right\}=0.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\min\left\{x-m(x),c^{-1}\Phi(x)\right\}=0
\]
is itself equivalent to the complementarity system, so minimizing its norm over \(\mathbb{R}^n\), or subject to \(x\geq m(x)\), gives an equivalent zero-residual optimization formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A GQVI over a translated nonnegative orthant is an implicit complementarity problem. The componentwise minimum of the slack and scaled mapping value vanishes exactly at complementary points, yielding constrained and unconstrained minimum-residual formulations.
assumptions_latex: x\geq m(x)\text{ for the stated gap-function bound and zero-gap equivalence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{GQVI}(K,\Phi)\iff0\leq x-m(x)\perp\Phi(x)\geq0\iff\min\{x-m(x),c^{-1}\Phi(x)\}=0.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularized gap certificate for a generalized quasi-variational inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the quadratic regularized gap for a GQVI and states its nonnegativity, attainment, and zero-gap characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}_{K}\Phi\) and \(c>0\), define
\[
\theta_c(x,v):=\max_{y\in K(x)}\left\{v^\top(x-y)-\frac c2\|y-x\|^2\right\}.
\]
If \(K(x)\neq\varnothing\) is closed, this maximum is attained and \(\theta_c(x,v)\geq0\). If, in addition, \(K(x)\) is convex, then
\[
\theta_c(x,v)=0\iff v^\top(y-x)\geq0\quad\forall y\in K(x).
\]
Thus \((x,v)\in\operatorname{gph}_{K}\Phi\) solves \(\operatorname{GQVI}(K,\Phi)\) exactly when \(\theta_c(x,v)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible GQVI pair, the regularized gap maximizes a linear violation term minus a quadratic term over K(x). A nonempty closed value K(x) ensures attainment and nonnegativity; convexity makes zero gap equivalent to the variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: K(x)\text{ is convex for the zero-gap equivalence}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta_c(x,v)\geq0,\qquad \theta_c(x,v)=0\iff v^\top(y-x)\geq0\ \forall y\in K(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean Regularized Gap Function and VI Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Euclidean regularized gap and records its smoothness boundary and zero-set characterization on the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(G:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be \(C^1\), and fix \(\alpha\ge 0\). Define \[g_\alpha(x):=\max_{y\in K}\left\{G(x)^T(x-y)-\frac{\alpha}{2}\|y-x\|^2\right\}.\] For every \(x\in K\), \(g_\alpha(x)\ge0\), and \[u\in\operatorname{SOL}(G,K)\iff u\in K\text{ and }g_\alpha(u)=0\iff u\in\arg\min_{x\in K}g_\alpha(x)\text{ and }g_\alpha(u)=0.\] When \(\alpha>0\), \(g_\alpha\) is continuously differentiable; at \(\alpha=0\), the resulting gap function need not be Fréchet differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously differentiable VI map on a closed convex set, the regularized gap maximizes the linearized VI residual minus a Euclidean quadratic term. It is nonnegative on the feasible set, vanishes there exactly at VI solutions, and is continuously differentiable for positive regularization, whereas the unregularized gap need not be Fréchet differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g_\alpha(x)\ge0\ (x\in K),\quad g_\alpha(u)=0\iff u\in\operatorname{SOL}(G,K),\quad \alpha>0\Rightarrow g_\alpha\in C^1.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-metric proximal regularization in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in C\), define \[g_{c,M}(x):=\max_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{c}{2}\|x-y\|_M^2\right\},\qquad \|z\|_M^2:=\langle Mz,z\rangle.\] Its unique maximizer is \[y_{c,M}(x)=P_C^M\left(x-c^{-1}M^{-1}F(x)\right).\] Moreover, \[g_{c,M}(x)\geq0,\qquad g_{c,M}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname{Sol}(C,F).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite metric defines a proximal regularized gap whose unique maximizer is a metric projection and whose feasible zeros are exactly the variational-inequality solutions.
assumptions_latex: \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal gap is attained at \(P_C^M(x-c^{-1}M^{-1}F(x))\), is nonnegative on \(C\), and vanishes exactly at VI solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman Gap Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman regularization with divergence oriented from the trial point to the base point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,y\in C\), define \[D_h(y,x):=h(y)-h(x)-\langle\nabla h(x),y-x\rangle.\] For \(x\in C\), define the extended-real Bregman gap by \[g_{c,h}(x):=\sup_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-cD_h(y,x)\right\}.\] Then \[g_{c,h}(x)\geq0,\qquad g_{c,h}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in\operatorname{Sol}(C,F).\] If the supremum is attained, its maximizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Bregman gap penalizes trial points by a strictly convex Bregman divergence. It may be extended-valued, is nonnegative, and has exactly the variational-inequality solutions as feasible zeros; any attained maximizer is unique.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is differentiable and strictly convex on an open set containing \(C\), and \(c>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in C\), \(g_{c,h}(x)\geq0\), and \(g_{c,h}(x)=0\) exactly when \(x\) solves \(\operatorname{VI}(C,F)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bregman–Proximal Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic Bregman generators recover fixed-metric proximal gaps exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h_M(z):=\frac12\langle Mz,z\rangle\), the associated Bregman divergence is \[D_{h_M}(y,x)=\frac12\langle M(y-x),y-x\rangle=\frac12\|y-x\|_M^2.\] Consequently, for every \(x\in C\), \[g_{c,h_M}(x)=\sup_{y\in C}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac{c}{2}\|x-y\|_M^2\right\}=g_{c,M}(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic generator induced by a positive-definite matrix, the Bregman divergence is one half of the squared metric norm, so the Bregman gap equals the fixed-metric proximal gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{h_M}(y,x)=\frac12\|y-x\|_M^2\) and \(g_{c,h_M}(x)=g_{c,M}(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Continuity, exactness, and gradient of the D-gap function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuity, nonnegativity, exact zero certificate, and conditional differentiability of the established D-gap function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be continuous, let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and convex, and let b>a>0. Then \theta_{ab} is continuous on \mathbb{R}^n, \theta_{ab}(x)\geq0 for every x, and \theta_{ab}(x)=0 if and only if x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For continuous F and closed convex K, the D-gap function is continuous and nonnegative, and its zeros are exactly the VI solutions. If F is continuously differentiable, the D-gap function is continuously differentiable with the stated gradient.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic bounds for the D-gap merit function

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationary-point characterization of D-gap solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between VI solvability and geometric conditions at a stationary point of the D-gap function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n be continuous, let K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n be closed and convex, let b>a>0, and let G be symmetric positive definite. If x is stationary for \theta_{ab} on \mathbb{R}^n, then the following are equivalent: (i) x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F); (ii) T_{ab}(x;K,F)\subseteq F(x)^\perp; (iii) for every d, \bigl[d\in T_{ab}(x;K,F)\ \text{and}\ JF(x)^Td\in-T_{ab}(x;K,F)^*\bigr]\Rightarrow d^TF(x)=0. In addition, the two conclusions identified as parts (a) and (b) of the referenced preceding corollary remain valid when T_c(x;K,F) is replaced by T_{ab}(x;K,F).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a stationary point of the D-gap function, solving the variational inequality is equivalent both to containment of the associated T_ab set in the orthogonal complement of F(x) and to the stated implication involving its dual cone and the transposed Jacobian. The theorem also transfers two preceding corollary conclusions from T_c to T_ab.
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is a stationary point of }\theta_{ab}\text{ on }\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\iff T_{ab}(x;K,F)\subseteq F(x)^\perp\iff\Bigl(\forall d,\ [d\in T_{ab}(x;K,F)\land JF(x)^Td\in-T_{ab}(x;K,F)^*]\Rightarrow d^TF(x)=0\Bigr),\text{ together with the stated }T_c\mapsto T_{ab}\text{ transfer of the preceding corollary's parts (a) and (b).}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternative sufficient conditions for global coercivity: quantitative monotonicity of the mapping or boundedness of the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex and let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be continuous. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local D-gap error bound at a semistable VI solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local solution-distance estimate and its stated positive-definiteness consequence for the second-order generalized differential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) be Lipschitz continuous in a neighborhood of a semistable solution \(x^*\) of \(\operatorname{VI}(K,F)\). For \(b>a>0\), there exist \(\eta>0\) and a neighborhood \(\mathcal N\) of \(x^*\) such that \[\lVert x-x^*\rVert\leq\eta\sqrt{\theta_{ab}(x)}\quad\forall x\in\mathcal N.\] Consequently, \[d^THd>0\quad\forall d\neq0,\quad\forall H\in\partial_d^2\theta_{ab}(x^*).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a semistable VI solution where F is locally Lipschitz, distance to that solution is bounded by a constant times the square root of the D-gap merit value. Every matrix in the stated second-order generalized differential at the solution is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained D-Gap Merit Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-space VI, where the D-gap reduces to a scaled nonlinear-equation residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\mathbb{R}^n\), \[g_c(x)=\frac{1}{2c}\|F(x)\|^2.\] Hence, for \(0<a<b\), \[G_{a,b}(x):=g_a(x)-g_b(x)=\frac{b-a}{2ab}\|F(x)\|^2\geq0.\] Its zero set is \[\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:G_{a,b}(x)=0\}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:F(x)=0\}.\] If \(F\) has a root, the minimum value of \(G_{a,b}\) is zero and its global minimizers are exactly the roots of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the full space, the D-gap is a positive multiple of the squared operator residual. Its zeros are exactly the roots of the operator; when roots exist, they are precisely its global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_{a,b}(x)=\frac{b-a}{2ab}\|F(x)\|^2\), and its zero set is exactly the root set of \(F\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unconstrained D-Gap Merit Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a difference of regularized gaps and gives its global-minimum certificate and orthant NCP specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed scalars \(\beta>\alpha>0\), define \[h_{\alpha\beta}(x):=g_\beta(x)-g_\alpha(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^n.\] Then \[u\in\operatorname{SOL}(G,K)\iff u\in\arg\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}h_{\alpha\beta}(x)\text{ and }h_{\alpha\beta}(u)=0.\] If \(\beta=1/\alpha\) and \(K=\mathbb{R}_+^n\), this merit function reduces to the implicit Lagrangian function for the nonlinear complementarity problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For beta greater than alpha greater than zero, the unconstrained D-gap merit is the beta-regularized gap minus the alpha-regularized gap. Its zero-valued global minimizers are exactly the VI solutions. With reciprocal parameters and the nonnegative orthant, it reduces to the NCP implicit Lagrangian.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Jacobian Sign Characterization of NCP D-Gap Stationary-Point Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The index sets \(\mathcal C,\mathcal P,\mathcal N\) are those determined by \(x\) and \(\varphi_v(x)\). The final S-matrix clause is preserved at the extract's reference level because condition (10.3.17) is not expanded in the supplied item.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuously differentiable, let \(b>a>0\), and let \(x\) be an unconstrained stationary point of \(\theta_{ab}^{\mathrm{ncp}}\). Then \(x\) solves \(\operatorname{NCP}(F)\) if and only if, for every \(z\ne0\) satisfying \(z_{\mathcal C}=0\), \(z_{\mathcal P}>0\), and \(z_{\mathcal N}<0\), there exists \(y\ne0\) satisfying \(y_{\mathcal C}=0\), \(y_{\mathcal P}\ge0\), and \(y_{\mathcal N}\le0\), such that \(z^TJF(x)y>0\). In particular, if \(\begin{bmatrix}J_{\mathcal P}F_{\mathcal P}(x)&-J_{\mathcal N}F_{\mathcal P}(x)\\-J_{\mathcal P}F_{\mathcal N}(x)&J_{\mathcal N}F_{\mathcal N}(x)\end{bmatrix}\) is an S-matrix, then the source's condition \((10.3.17)\) holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stationary point of the unconstrained NCP D-gap merit function solves the NCP exactly when every nonzero vector with the prescribed strict signs admits a nonzero vector with the corresponding weak signs that has a positive Jacobian bilinear product. The displayed signed Jacobian block being an S-matrix is additionally sufficient for the referenced condition (10.3.17).
assumptions_latex: x\text{ is an unconstrained stationary point of }\theta_{ab}^{\mathrm{ncp}}
\mathcal C,\mathcal P,\mathcal N\text{ are defined with respect to }x\text{ and }\varphi_v(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\in\operatorname{SOL}(\operatorname{NCP}(F))\iff \forall z\ne0\;[z_{\mathcal C}=0,\ z_{\mathcal P}>0,\ z_{\mathcal N}<0\Rightarrow\exists y\ne0:\ y_{\mathcal C}=0,\ y_{\mathcal P}\ge0,\ y_{\mathcal N}\le0,\ z^TJF(x)y>0]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complementarity and derivative-sign properties of the scalar function underlying the unconstrained NCP D-gap model.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Affine-Constraint Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete recession-direction boundary for D-gap coercivity on an unbounded affine set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\mathbb{R}^2\), \(F(x_1,x_2)=(x_1,0)\), and \(0<a<b\). For \(g_c(x)=\sup_{y\in K}\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\tfrac c2\|x-y\|^2\}\) and \(D_{a,b}=g_a-g_b\), one has
\[
D_{a,b}(x)=\frac12\left(\frac1a-\frac1b\right)x_1^2.
\]
The VI solution set and the zero set of \(D_{a,b}\) are both \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:x_1=0\}\). Every nonempty sublevel set of \(D_{a,b}\) is unbounded in the \(x_2\)-direction, so zero validity does not imply coercivity or bounded merit sublevels on this unbounded affine set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In this affine example, the D-gap identifies the VI solutions exactly but is constant along an unbounded direction, making every nonempty sublevel unbounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{a,b}(x)=\tfrac12(a^{-1}-b^{-1})x_1^2\), and every nonempty sublevel set is unbounded in the \(x_2\)-direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Model Linearized Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional quadratic linearization using the symmetric Jacobian part.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in K\), let \(H_x=\tfrac12(F'(x)+F'(x)^{\mathsf T})\). If \(H_x\) is positive semidefinite on \(\operatorname{span}(K-K)\) and the displayed quadratic program has a finite attained minimum, the affine-model linearized gap is
\[
\ell(x):=-\min_{d\in K-x}\left\{\langle F(x),d\rangle+\frac12\langle d,H_xd\rangle\right\}.
\]
It is the negative optimal value of the convex quadratic affine model over feasible displacements and satisfies \(\ell(x)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine-model linearized gap is the negative finite minimum of the convex local quadratic model over feasible displacements.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic-model minimum is finite and attained
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(x)=-\min_{d\in K-x}\{\langle F(x),d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle d,H_xd\rangle\}\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric part of the derivative at x

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Model Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise zero certificate under convexity of the local quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
q_x(d)=\langle F(x),d\rangle+\frac12\langle d,H_xd\rangle,
\qquad
\ell(x)=-\min_{d\in K-x}q_x(d).
\]
If \(H_x\) is positive semidefinite on \(\operatorname{span}(K-K)\) and the minimum is finite and attained, then
\[
\ell(x)=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\quad\text{for every }y\in K.
\]
Thus \(\ell(x)=0\) is an exact pointwise certificate for the original variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a well-posed convex local quadratic model, the linearized gap is zero exactly at points satisfying the original variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: The quadratic-model minimum defining \(\ell(x)\) is finite and attained
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell(x)=0\iff \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\) for every \(y\in K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\), define the orthant implicit-Lagrangian value by
\[
L_\alpha(x)=\max_{y\ge0}\left\{\langle F(x),x-y\rangle-\frac\alpha2\|x-y\|^2\right\}.
\]
Its unique maximizer is \(y_\alpha=P_+(x-\alpha^{-1}F(x))\), and therefore
\[
L_\alpha(x)=\langle F(x),r_\alpha(x)\rangle-\frac\alpha2\|r_\alpha(x)\|^2.
\]
The projection characterization yields \(L_\alpha(x)\ge0\), with equality exactly when \(r_\alpha(x)=0\), equivalently when \(x\ge0\), \(F(x)\ge0\), and \(\langle x,F(x)\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing the regularized orthant Lagrangian gives a nonnegative projected-residual merit function whose zeros solve the NCP.
knowledge_statements.title: NCP Implicit Lagrangian

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is zero-valid exactly when \(M(x)=0\iff x\in S\) for every \(x\in K\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
S=\left\{x\in K:\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\text{ for every }y\in K\right\}.
\]
A nonnegative function \(M:K\to[0,\infty]\) has the zero-characterization property for the variational inequality precisely when
\[
M^{-1}(\{0\})=S,
\]
or equivalently, for every \(x\in K\), \(M(x)=0\) if and only if \(x\in S\). Nonnegativity and vanishing at all solutions alone are insufficient: exclusion of zeros in \(K\setminus S\) is an independent required implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A merit certificate is zero-valid exactly when its zero set equals the variational-inequality solution set.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Characterization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth convex minimizers and Stampacchia–Minty inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained minimization of a differentiable convex functional on a closed convex subset of a reflexive Banach space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V\) be a reflexive Banach space, let \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subset V\) be closed and convex, and let \(F:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and Gâteaux differentiable with continuous derivative. For every \(u\in\mathcal C\), the following are equivalent: \[F(u)=\inf_{w\in\mathcal C}F(w);\qquad \langle F'(u),v-u\rangle\ge0\ \ \forall v\in\mathcal C;\qquad \langle F'(v),v-u\rangle\ge0\ \ \forall v\in\mathcal C.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper lower-semicontinuous convex functional with continuous Gâteaux derivative on a nonempty closed convex subset of a reflexive Banach space, a feasible point is a minimizer if and only if it satisfies the Stampacchia variational inequality, equivalently the Minty variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: V\text{ is a reflexive Banach space}
\varnothing\ne\mathcal C\subset V\text{ is closed and convex}
F:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}
F\text{ is Gâteaux differentiable and }F'\text{ is continuous}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(u)=\inf_{w\in\mathcal C}F(w)\iff \bigl[\langle F'(u),v-u\rangle\ge0\ \forall v\in\mathcal C\bigr]\iff \bigl[\langle F'(v),v-u\rangle\ge0\ \forall v\in\mathcal C\bigr]

children.top_down_role: Quantitative regimes relating certificate magnitude to solution error.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Error-Bound Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local residual error bounds transferred to comparable merit certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and define
\[
S=\{x\in K:\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\ge0\ \text{for every }y\in K\},
\qquad
R(x)=x-P_K(x-F(x)).
\]
Assume \(S\ne\varnothing\). If a neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\), constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+>0\), and \(p>0\) satisfy
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\|R(x)\|,
\qquad
c_-\|R(x)\|^p\le M(x)\le c_+\|R(x)\|^p
\]
for every \(x\in U\cap K\), then \(M\) is zero-valid on \(U\cap K\) and
\[
\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa c_-^{-1/p}M(x)^{1/p}
\]
for every \(x\in U\cap K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a closed convex VI domain, a local natural-residual error bound together with positive two-sided merit comparability makes the certificate locally zero-valid and quantitatively controls distance to the solution set.
assumptions_latex: On a neighborhood \(U\) of \(S\), \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\|R(x)\|\) and \(c_-\|R(x)\|^p\le M(x)\le c_+\|R(x)\|^p\) for constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+>0\) and \(p>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in U\cap K\), \(M(x)=0\iff x\in S\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa c_-^{-1/p}M(x)^{1/p}\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of zero validity when a residual weight can vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The unconstrained variational inequality for \(F(x)=x\) has the unique solution \(S=\{0\}\), and its natural residual is \(R(x)=x\). Consider the nonnegative weighted residual certificate
\[
M(x)=(x-1)^2R(x)^2=x^2(x-1)^2.
\]
Although every solution satisfies \(M(x)=0\), the converse fails because \(M(1)=0\) while \(F(1)=1\ne0\). Thus a merit construction of the form \(w(x)\|R(x)\|^2\) can acquire spurious zeros when strict positivity of the weight \(w\) away from the solution set is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual multiplied by a vanishing weight can have zeros at nonsolutions, even though it remains nonnegative and vanishes at every solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Spurious-Zero Failure Boundary

children.title: Zero-Valid but Nonmetric Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes retaining zero characterization without a useful error bound.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^{-1}(0)=\{0\}\), but no global constant \(C\) satisfies \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le C M(x)^{1/2}\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero validity without any global residual-to-distance error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the unconstrained variational inequality \(F(x)=0\), take \(F(x)=x/(1+x^2)\). Its solution set is \(S=\{0\}\), and
\[
M(x)=|F(x)|^2=\frac{x^2}{(1+x^2)^2}
\]
is nonnegative with \(M(x)=0\) exactly on \(S\). Nevertheless, a global estimate \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le C M(x)^{1/2}\) would require
\[
|x|\le C\frac{|x|}{1+x^2}
\]
for all \(x\), which is impossible. Hence exact zero characterization does not by itself make a certificate a global error metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate may identify solutions exactly while becoming arbitrarily small far from them, so zero validity alone gives no global distance control.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Valid but Nonmetric Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(K=\mathbb{R}\) and the constant mapping \(F(x)=1\), the classical primal gap is
\[
g(x)=\sup_{y\in\mathbb{R}}(x-y).
\]
Taking \(y\to-\infty\) shows that \(g(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\). Thus the unregularized supremum gap need not be a finite-valued merit function on an unbounded feasible set. Finiteness requires boundedness of \(K\), suitable recession-direction conditions, or a coercive regularization term in the maximized expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an unbounded feasible set, the classical supremum gap can be infinite everywhere unless recession directions are controlled or regularized.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Gap-Function Pathology

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth squared-residual merit with a stationary nonsolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the unconstrained variational inequality on \(K=\mathbb{R}\), solutions are zeros of \(F\). Let \(F(x)=x^2+1\), so the problem has no solution, and define
\[
M(x)=\frac12|F(x)|^2=\frac12(x^2+1)^2.
\]
Then
\[
M'(x)=2x(x^2+1),
\]
so \(M'(0)=0\), whereas \(M(0)=1/2>0\) and \(F(0)=1\ne0\). Consequently first-order stationarity of a smooth merit function does not, without additional structural assumptions, certify solution of the underlying variational inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth squared-residual merit function can have a stationary point with positive residual, so merit stationarity need not imply VI solvability.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationary Nonsolution Pathology

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing merit along an unbounded sequence despite a unique finite solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The unconstrained variational inequality for \(F(x)=x/(1+x^2)\) has the unique solution \(S=\{0\}\). Its squared-residual merit function
\[
M(x)=\frac12|F(x)|^2=\frac{x^2}{2(1+x^2)^2}
\]
is zero-valid. However, for \(x_k=k\),
\[
|x_k|\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
M(x_k)=\frac{k^2}{2(1+k^2)^2}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus every positive sublevel of \(M\) contains an unbounded tail, and sequences with vanishing merit need not be bounded or approach the solution set. Coercivity or bounded-level-set assumptions are therefore separate from zero validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-valid merit can tend to zero along an escaping sequence, so vanishing merit does not ensure bounded iterates or convergence to solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Level-Set Escape

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose $w^0\in S$ sufficiently close to a solution $\bar w$ of $\operatorname{VI}(F,S)$. For $k=0,1,2,\ldots$, stop if $w^k$ solves $\operatorname{VI}(F,S)$. Otherwise compute a solution $w^{k+1}$ closest to $w^k$ of the linearized variational inequality: $w^{k+1}\in S$ and $\bigl(F(w^k)+F'(w^k)(w^{k+1}-w^k)\bigr)^T(v-w^{k+1})\ge0$ for every $v\in S$. For $k\ge1$, $w^k=w^{k-1}$ implies that the stopping condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin in S sufficiently near a solution. At each iteration, solve the variational inequality obtained by affine-linearizing F and select its solution closest to the current iterate. Stop when the current point solves the original VI; an unchanged consecutive iterate provides this certificate.
assumptions_latex: w^0\text{ is sufficiently close to }\bar w
F'(w^k)\text{ exists at each iterate where a step is computed}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^{k+1}\in S,\qquad \bigl(F(w^k)+F'(w^k)(w^{k+1}-w^k)\bigr)^T(v-w^{k+1})\ge0\quad\forall v\in S,\quad w^{k+1}\text{ chosen closest to }w^k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of the Euclidean projected-forward VI iteration when positive steps are uniformly bounded away from zero and below twice the cocoercivity constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be cocoercive on \(K\) with constant \(c\), and suppose \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\neq\varnothing\). knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Metric Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed positive-definite metric version of the projected forward iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in C\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and an iteration limit \(K\in\mathbb{N}\), compute for \(k=0,\ldots,K-1\)
\[
x_{k+1}=P_C^A\bigl(x_k-\alpha A^{-1}F(x_k)\bigr),\qquad
P_C^A(z)=\mathop{\operatorname{argmin}}_{y\in C}\frac12\|y-z\|_A^2.
\]
Terminate when \(\|r_A(x_k)\|_A\leq\varepsilon\); otherwise return \(x_K\). For every \(x\in C\),
\[
r_A(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use one fixed positive-definite metric for every projected forward step. A zero fixed-point residual is equivalent to solving the variational inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:C\to H\).
\(A:H\to H\) is bounded and self-adjoint, with \(mI\preceq A\preceq \overline m I\) for constants \(0<m\leq\overline m<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in C\) solves the variational inequality exactly when \(r_A(x)=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), select \(M_k\) and \(\alpha_k\), then set
\[
x_{k+1}=P_C^{M_k}\bigl(x_k-\alpha_kM_k^{-1}F(x_k)\bigr),\qquad
P_C^{M_k}(z)=\mathop{\operatorname{argmin}}_{y\in C}\frac12\langle M_k(y-z),y-z\rangle.
\]
Stop when \(\|r_k\|_{M_k}\leq\varepsilon\), or return the last iterate at a prescribed iteration limit. Uniform spectral bounds make all iteration norms equivalent to the ambient norm but do not alone control temporal metric variation.

children.title: Metric Adaptation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes governing transitions from fixed to adaptive metrics.

assumptions_latex: \(M_k\) is self-adjoint and \(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\) for fixed positive constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed alternatives define standard controlled metric-adaptation regimes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common quantitative regimes that keep metric adaptation compatible with variable-metric quasi-Fejér analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A metric sequence has summably controlled relative growth when
\[
M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k\quad\text{for every }k,
\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.
\]
A stronger two-sided regime requires
\[
(1+\eta_k)^{-1}M_k\preceq M_{k+1}\preceq(1+\eta_k)M_k.
\]
An additive bounded-variation regime instead requires \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|M_{k+1}-M_k\|<\infty\). Any one of these conditions, together with uniform spectral bounds, quantitatively limits cumulative changes of projection geometry; they are alternative predicates, not simultaneous requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric adaptation is controlled by summable one-sided growth, summable two-sided relative change, or finite total operator-norm variation.
knowledge_statements.title: Metric Adaptation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three predicates are mathematically plausible and fit the condition leaf, but no source is supplied for their status as standard variable-metric adaptation regimes.

children.title: Variable-Metric Stability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Stability limitations associated with changing projection metrics.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Metric-error decay need not imply ambient-norm decay once uniform coercivity is removed.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of norm control when variable metrics approach singularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The matrices \(M_k\) are positive definite for every finite \(k\), but no constant \(m>0\) satisfies \(mI\preceq M_k\) for all \(k\). For the constant sequence \(e_k=(1,0)\),
\[
\|e_k\|_{M_k}=\frac{1}{k+1}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\|e_k\|=1.
\]
Thus convergence of residuals or errors measured only in the changing metric cannot be converted into convergence in the ambient norm without uniform coercivity. This example isolates a stability boundary independently of any particular operator or projection update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerating metrics can make a fixed nonzero error appear to vanish, so uniform coercivity is essential for translating metric estimates into ambient convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Projection Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected forward iteration with underrelaxation or overrelaxation in the ambient Hilbert-space metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x_0\in H\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and an iteration limit \(K\in\mathbb{N}\). For \(k=0,\ldots,K-1\), compute
\[
p_k=P_C\bigl(x_k-\alpha F(x_k)\bigr),
\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+\lambda_k(p_k-x_k).
\]
Terminate when \(\|x_k-p_k\|\leq\varepsilon\); otherwise return \(x_K\). Values \(0<\lambda_k<1\) give underrelaxation, \(\lambda_k=1\) gives the basic update, and \(1<\lambda_k<2\) gives overrelaxation. For every \(x\in H\),
\[
x=P_C(x-\alpha F(x))
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
x\in C\ \text{and}\ \langle F(x),y-x\rangle\geq0\ \text{for every }y\in C.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax the projected-forward displacement by a factor between zero and two. A zero projected residual is equivalent to a variational-inequality solution, while overrelaxed intermediate iterates need not remain feasible.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:H\to H\).
The stepsize satisfies \(\alpha>0\), and \(0<\lambda_k<2\) for every iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed point of the relaxed update solves the variational inequality on \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Method Noncontraction Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the usual strong-monotonicity contraction estimate for projected forward maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(T_\alpha=P_C\circ(I-\alpha F)\). If \(F\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz, then for all \(x,y\in C\),
\[
\|T_\alpha x-T_\alpha y\|^2
\leq\bigl(1-2\alpha\mu+\alpha^2L^2\bigr)\|x-y\|^2.
\]
Thus this bound is contractive when \(0<\alpha<2\mu/L^2\). Mere monotonicity does not ensure nonexpansiveness: for \(C=\mathbb{R}^2\) and \(F=J\), where \(J(a,b)=(-b,a)\),
\[
\|(I-\alpha J)u\|=\sqrt{1+\alpha^2}\,\|u\|
\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb{R}^2.
\]
Consequently, this monotone Lipschitz example is expansive for every \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong monotonicity gives a contraction interval for the projected forward map. Under mere monotonicity, a skew rotation provides an example in which every positive forward stepsize is expansive.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(C\subset H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(F:C\to H\).
For the contraction estimate, \(F\) is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone and \(L\)-Lipschitz with \(\mu>0\) and \(L>0\).
For the boundary example, \(H=C=\mathbb{R}^2\) and \(F=J\), where \(J(a,b)=(-b,a)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elementary contraction guarantee is available for \(\mu>0\) in the stated stepsize interval but can fail completely under mere monotonicity.

\(F:C\to H\) is monotone: \(\langle F(x)-F(y),x-y\rangle\geq0\) for all \(x,y\in C\).
The solution set \(S\) of the variational inequality is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every solution belongs to every valid correction halfspace generated from a feasible trial point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone-operator setting underlying projection–contraction separation and correction steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \(x\in C\), \(\beta>0\), and \(y=P_C(x-\beta F(x))\), define \(d=(x-y)-\beta(F(x)-F(y))\). The projection inequality and monotonicity imply that every \(x^\star\in S\) satisfies
\[
\langle d,x^\star-y\rangle\leq0.
\]
Consequently, the halfspace \(H(x,y)=\{z\in H:\langle d,z-y\rangle\leq0\}\) contains \(S\). This containment is the monotone-regime invariant used by projection–contraction methods; strict separation additionally requires a positive margin at the current point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotonicity ensures that the correction halfspace constructed from a projected trial point contains the entire solution set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: R-linear convergence of projection and proximal VI iterations under a local error bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three method-specific linear-convergence conclusions sharing nonemptiness and a local natural-residual error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose \(S=\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\neq\varnothing\) has a local error bound with the natural residual. (a) If \(F\) is cocoercive on \(K\) with modulus greater than \(1/2\), then, for every \(x^0\in K\), \(x^{k+1}=\Pi_K(x^k-F(x^k))\) converges to a point of \(S\) at least R-linearly. (b) If \(F\) is monotone and Lipschitz continuous on \(K\) with constant \(L>0\), then, for every \(c\in(0,1/L)\) and \(x^0\in K\), the iteration in which \(x^{k+1}\) is the unique solution of \(\operatorname{VI}(K,\mathbf I-x^k+cF)\) converges to a point of \(S\) at least R-linearly. (c) Let \(D\) be positive definite, \(Y=D_s^{1/2}K\), \(C=D_s^{-1/2}(D-D_s)D_s^{-1/2}\), and \(\widetilde F_D(y)=D_s^{-1/2}F(D_s^{-1/2}y)\). If \(\widetilde F_D-C\) is cocoercive on \(Y\) with modulus greater than \(1/2\) and \(\|C\|<1\), then, for every \(x^0\in K\), \(x^{k+1}=\Pi_{K,D}(x^k-D^{-1}F(x^k))\) converges to a point of \(S\) at least R-linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty VI solution set with a local natural-residual error bound yields R-linear convergence for three schemes: ordinary projection under cocoercivity exceeding one half, proximal point under monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity with c below 1/L, and asymmetric projection under the stated transformed cocoercivity and asymmetry-norm conditions.
assumptions_latex: S\text{ has a local error bound with the natural residual}
\text{In (c), }D\succ0,\ \widetilde F_D-C\text{ is cocoercive on }D_s^{1/2}K\text{ with modulus }>1/2,\ \|C\|<1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Each corresponding sequence converges to an element of }\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\text{ at least R-linearly}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in C\). At iteration \(k\), form a projected trial point \(y_k\), a normal \(d_k\), and the halfspace \(H_k\). Compute
\[
\widehat{x}_{k+1}=P_{H_k}(x_k)
=x_k-\frac{[\langle d_k,x_k-y_k\rangle]_+}{\|d_k\|^2}d_k,
\qquad
x_{k+1}=P_C\bigl(x_k+\gamma_k(\widehat{x}_{k+1}-x_k)\bigr).
\]
Stop when the trial residual \(\|x_k-y_k\|\leq\varepsilon\), or return the final iterate. Omitting the final projection is a valid unconstrained-correction variant when feasibility of intermediate iterates is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct a halfspace containing all solutions, project toward it with relaxation, and optionally reproject onto the feasible set.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is monotone on the nonempty closed convex set \(C\).
The line search verifies \(\beta\langle F(x)-F(y),x-y\rangle\leq\sigma\|x-y\|^2\) for some \(0\leq\sigma<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((d,y)\) is a directly checkable separating-halfspace certificate unless \(x=y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable containment and strict-separation certificate for a projection–contraction correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Monotonicity and the projection inequality certify
\[
\langle d,x^\star-y\rangle\leq0\quad\text{for every }x^\star\in S,
\]
so \(S\subset H\). The line-search inequality independently certifies
\[
\langle d,x-y\rangle
=\|x-y\|^2-\beta\langle F(x)-F(y),x-y\rangle
\geq(1-\sigma)\|x-y\|^2.
\]
Therefore, if \(x\neq y\), the current point lies strictly outside \(H\), while every solution lies inside it. Both claims are checkable using the computed pair \((x,y)\), operator values, and the scalar line-search test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computable line-search margin proves that the correction halfspace contains every solution and strictly excludes the current nonsolution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fejér monotonicity and asymptotic properties of hyperplane projection iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intermediate convergence properties of Algorithm 12.1.12 under solution-relative pseudomonotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, and let \(F:K\to\mathbb{R}^n\) be continuous and pseudomonotone on \(K\) with respect to \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\). If \(\{x^k\}\) is generated by Algorithm 12.1.12, then: (i) for every \(x^*\in\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\), the sequence \(\{\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert\}\) is nonincreasing and convergent; (ii) \(\{x^k\}\) is bounded; (iii) \(\lim_{k\to\infty}F(z^k)^T(x^k-z^k)=0\); and (iv) if an accumulation point \(\bar x\) of \(\{x^k\}\) belongs to \(\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)\), then \(x^k\to\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the specified hyperplane projection algorithm, the iterates are Fejér monotone relative to every solution and bounded, the separation product tends to zero, and any solution accumulation point is the limit of the entire sequence.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ is pseudomonotone on }K\text{ with respect to }\operatorname{SOL}(K,F)
